spec.title: Seat the Phase 4 blanket-staging ban in a PreToolUse hook
spec.problem: The Phase 4 tracked-write isolation block in plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:812 and in all nine agents/*.md files ends by admitting its own gap: the commit-hygiene rule (read git status --porcelain, stage explicit paths only, never `git commit -a` / `git add -A` / `git add .`) is 'the only one of these rules sited at the actual ship event' and 'nothing mechanically enforces it either'. #19 established the harm (four Phase 4 reviewers corrupted each other's mutation batteries in one shared worktree; SecOps rated a blanket fix-round commit HIGH because it would ship a narrowed halting control) and shipped prose. Nothing reads the prose. This is evidence.md rule 19 turned on this repo's own contract: a written expectation no code reads is a comment. #66/#100 closed the identical shape at SubagentStop; this closes it at PreToolUse.
spec.root_cause: The rule is sited at a tool call (a Bash invocation of git) and the plugin declares no hook at that event. hooks/hooks.json carries exactly three events (SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStop); `grep -rn PreToolUse plugins/pipeline/` returns zero hits across every file type.
spec.rework_note: Round 3 rework, 2026-09-01, after a third Phase 2 pass (DevOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES with zero blockers/majors, DBA and SecOps REQUEST_CHANGES). Both reviewers independently confirmed seam_extension_ruling correct on its own reasoning, so the core tension is settled and this round is narrower. ONE FINDING WAS A REAL ENGINEERING PROBLEM RATHER THAN SPEC WORDING: R6's seam extension forces a module cycle with a shipped guard, because plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs:71 already imports from validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs. I reproduced it on the REAL 16-module graph and verified the leaf-module fix closes it (numbers in measured_state and R6). Also this round: clause (ii) of the ruling was overstated and is corrected; the undatable-record rule was safe in one direction and manufactured a deny in the other, found independently by both reviewers; the marker precedence path was never mentioned in the spec although R16 mandates using it; R17 cited the four lines that refuse its own shape; hooks.json's timeout is SECONDS not milliseconds; the 'non-string updated_at' cell asserted a divergence that does not exist; and R7's 'floor not rule' clause was never checked, with combined short flags the live example.
spec.seam_extension_ruling: RULING: option A, extend the shared seam, scoped ADDITIVELY. Recorded here rather than in a summary because the reasoning is the deliverable, and because a later reader will otherwise re-open it. THE ARGUMENT FOR B IS A FALSE EQUIVALENCE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE RULING. B says: activeIssueDir's newest-mtime resolution is already accepted at SubagentStop, so accepting it here imports a known limitation rather than a new one. The two sites are not alike in the way that matters. (i) THE PREMISE HOLDS AT ONE SITE AND NOT THE OTHER. The function's own header justifies the mtime scan on 'a session owns exactly one active issue'. A SubagentStop fires inside a pipeline run, where that is usually true. PreToolUse fires on every Bash call in every session in the project, including sessions that own no issue at all, so the premise is not merely unreliable there - it is routinely false. (ii) THE FAILURE DIRECTION INVERTS. At SubagentStop a wrong pick validates an artifact this session did not write. CORRECTED IN ROUND 3, because the round-2 wording said 'and the whole surrounding machinery is fail-open and advisory' and that is contradicted by the code it cites: hooks/subagent-stop.sh is fail-open for TOOLING gaps only and passes a real decision:block straight through, and plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:292-294 says the scoping exists precisely so a foreign artifact cannot 'block a stop for work the session never touched'. So a wrong pick at SubagentStop can REFUSE A CORRECT STOP. The ruling stands on clauses (i) and (iii), which both reviewers verified; what does not stand is the implication that the deferred SubagentStop migration is a harmless latent improvement. It is a live refuses-correct-work defect in its own right, and the follow-on is #109, written with that direction stated rather than filed as a nice-to-have. At PreToolUse a wrong pick DENIES A TOOL CALL. That is refusing correct work - the claim-MORE direction evidence.md's ship-or-block line says closes now, not later - and both reviewers measured it live with no adversary: with two runs in flight, a legitimate Phase 3 `git commit -a` on run A is denied because run B is newer and sits at 4-review. An accepted limitation is accepted at a site where its direction is harmless; carrying it to a site where the direction inverts is a new defect wearing an old defect's clearance. (iii) B ALSO FORCES A CHOICE BETWEEN TWO THINGS THIS ISSUE EXISTS TO REFUSE. Under B the implementer either re-derives the predicate privately, which is #66's drift class and exactly what R14 forbids, or ships R4 as a guarantee that does not hold, which is a claim-MORE defect in the artifact whose entire subject is making a contract honest. Trading a real drift hazard for a false guarantee is the worst available outcome, and it is the one B produces by default. SCOPE OF A, AND THE LIMIT ON IT. The extension is ADDITIVE ONLY: a new export supplying run-candidate resolution, with activeIssueDir's existing behaviour unchanged and its existing self-checks passing unmodified (AC27). This issue does NOT flip SubagentStop over to the new resolution, even though SubagentStop has the identical latent problem and the coordinator is right that fixing it there would be a genuine improvement. The reason is this issue's own subject: silently changing a shipped gate's behaviour as a side effect of a change reviewed for something else is the blanket-commit harm one level up, and I will not have this spec commit it while retiring a sentence about it. The SubagentStop migration is filed as a follow-on, named in out_of_scope, with this ruling as its rationale. WHAT A COSTS, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER: out_of_scope must widen to admit this specific export (it does, below), the diff grows a module SubagentStop imports from, and Phase 4 must verify the additive claim rather than assume it - which is what AC27 is for (round-4 wording cited AC30, which is the residual-text criterion; a reviewer following that pointer would have verified the wrong thing).
requirements: R1. Declare a PreToolUse hook in plugins/pipeline/hooks/hooks.json that reaches Bash tool calls, alongside the three existing events, and ship it with the plugin. It must carry an explicit bounded `timeout` EXPRESSED IN SECONDS. The unit is fixed by the runtime, not by the file's other entries: in Claude Code 2.1.85 the hook-exec path computes `E=H.timeout?H.timeout*1000:EL` with `EL=600000`, so the field is seconds and the implicit ceiling is 600 s. The three shipped entries (10000, 120000, 15000) are therefore 2.8 h, 33.3 h and 4.2 h - all ABOVE the platform's own default - so 'smaller than Stop's 120000' bounds nothing and must not be used as the comparison. The declared value must be strictly less than the platform default ceiling and justified against this spec's own baselines converted to seconds (66.68 ms node cold start plus one git subprocess on the escalation branch); a small single-digit number of seconds is the intended magnitude. The seconds/milliseconds defect in the three ALREADY-SHIPPED entries is #108 and is not fixed here.

R2. ORIGIN TERM. The gate's 'this call came from inside a subagent' term must be FALSE for every payload carrying no subagent identifier, whatever agent_type says. Claude Code 2.1.85's hook payload schema fixes this literally: agent_id is 'Subagent identifier. Present only when the hook fires from within a subagent (e.g., a tool called by an AgentTool worker). Absent for the main thread, even in --agent sessions. Use this field (not agent_type) to distinguish subagent calls from main-thread calls.' Re-derive: `strings -a <redacted-absolute-path> | grep -o 'agent_id:h[^;]\{0,300\}' | head -1`. HALVES: this REPLACES the origin term only. agent_type is still READ, for the attribution R12 requires, and that half is enforced by AC4 rather than left to intent.

R3. NO ROLE ALLOWLIST. Because R2 supplies origin, the deny population must not be an enumerated set of roles. Any subagent-originated call is in scope during a Phase 4 phase, whatever its agent_type spells or fails to spell. This is what makes the gate cover pipeline:design (dispatched under that literal, never 'design_review', which is only the shard key) and art_director, whose dispatched agent_type is fixed nowhere in plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md's Phase 4 block. CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST BE STATED WHERE READERS HIT IT, not merely accepted: this refuses blanket staging by subagents that are not pipeline panelists at all - a general-purpose Task worker, an adopting project's own agent - whenever a Phase 4 run is the resolved owner. That refusal is deliberate (narrowing it reintroduces the allowlist this requirement removes) and must appear in R21's replacement text and in the operator README.

R4. RUN-OWNERSHIP: THE MTIME DERIVATION IS NEVER AN OWNERSHIP SIGNAL. The phase the gate acts on must belong to the run the denied call belongs to, and must never be decided by which unrelated concurrent or abandoned run wrote a status.json most recently. THREE ROUNDS RUNNING (4, 5, 6) REINTRODUCED THAT DERIVATION IN A NEW SHAPE - as a selector among candidates, then as a tie-break, then as a 'select AMONG them, never outside them' clause whose only bound was the outside - so the rule is stated now as a prohibition rather than as an order with an exception. RESOLUTION, and there is no other branch: narrow by R5 to the in-flight candidate set. (1) ZERO candidates -> ABSTAIN. (2) EXACTLY ONE candidate -> that record is the owner. (3) TWO OR MORE candidates -> ONLY an explicit marker honoured under R25(a), naming one OF THAT SET, resolves the ambiguity; with no such marker the gate ABSTAINS, UNCONDITIONALLY - no tie-break, no newest-wins, no 'select among', and no distinction between a tied and an untied mtime, because mtime is not consulted in this branch at all. The mtime derivation therefore has NO role in ownership in any branch: in (2) the answer is already determined without it, and in (1) and (3) it is not consulted. R6's requirement that the new export distinguish a marker resolution from an inferred one is what makes this implementable - the gate consumes the marker resolution and discards the inferred one. MEASURED ON A REAL `git clone --no-hardlinks` OF THIS REPO, which is why the round-6 version had to go: the clone carries TWO in-flight records (98 at '4-review', 106) and the raw resolver returns `exp-script-test-coverage`, a record carrying a final_verdict that R5 excludes outright. Under round 6's clause (4) the newest in-flight candidate (98, at a Phase 4 phase) would have owned the deny and refused correct work in 106's session, on a fresh clone of this very repository. Under this rule the same root abstains.

R5. IN-FLIGHT PREDICATE, GRAIN FIXED ON THE FIELD NOT THE FILE, AND ASYMMETRIC ON DATABILITY. In-flight means: no `final_verdict`, AND `Date.parse(status.updated_at)` within `IN_FLIGHT_MS`. Both literals are fixed by this project's own authority: `plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs:188` (`export const IN_FLIGHT_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`) and `:548-552`. THE GRAIN IS `updated_at`, NOT FILE MTIME: a checkout, clone or sync refreshes every mtime while leaving `updated_at` intact, and measured on this repo's corpus copied to a scratch root and fully touched, the mtime grain yields 6 candidates against the field grain's 2 - a gate that would abstain forever after every clone, in the adopting-project deployment R18 protects. EVALUATION ORDER IS FIXED, because the two readings differ in the deny direction and round 4 found the spec did not say which. `final_verdict` is evaluated FIRST and excludes UNCONDITIONALLY; databability is asked only of records that are NOT concluded. Reason, NARROWED IN ROUND 6 because round 5 overstated it: `final_verdict` is a statement that needs no dating, and it is USUALLY a statement that the run is over. It is not always. DBA proved on this repo's own committed history that `current_phase` re-enters '4-review' for a delta round while a STALE `final_verdict` from the prior round is still attached (.pipeline/19 at commit c337579, mid-fix-round, final_verdict still set), so a genuinely live Phase 4 run can carry one. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS GATE IS A KNOWN RESIDUAL, DIRECTION NAMED: such a run is excluded from the candidate set, so the gate ABSTAINS where it would otherwise deny - claim-LESS, a silence, never a refusal of correct work. That is the safe direction and it is why this order still stands. The underlying status.json lifecycle defect predates and is broader than this issue and is tracked as #110; it is NOT fixed here, and R21 carries it as a named residual rather than leaving a reader to assume the exclusion is always correct; databability only matters when the question is 'is this recent?', which is a question worth asking only of an unconcluded record. The cross cell is real - a root holding one live datable '4-review' record plus one CONCLUDED record whose updated_at is unparseable yields ONE candidate under this order (and denies) versus TWO under the other (and abstains) - and the deny it produces is correct, because there genuinely is exactly one in-flight run and it is at a Phase 4 phase. The alternative reading also carries a cost it never states: the candidate set would be inflated permanently by any concluded record that ever loses a parseable updated_at, silencing the gate forever. R5's safety claim is therefore restated precisely: WITHIN THE UNCONCLUDED POPULATION the databability asymmetry can only ever remove denies, never add one; it makes no claim about the concluded population, which `final_verdict` has already excluded. THE DATABILITY RULE IS AN ASYMMETRY, and round 3 found the half that was missing. A record the gate cannot date (Date.parse yields NaN) must PREVENT narrowing - it counts toward the candidate set, so it can never shrink a set to one - and must NEVER ITSELF BE THE RESOLVED OWNER of a deny. Inclusion alone was unsafe in the direction the round-3 spec did not state: it can grow the set from zero to one, and R4 would then treat a record whose recency is by construction unknowable, i.e. an arbitrarily old abandoned run, as the owner and deny on its authority. Both reviewers found this independently. The asymmetry can only ever REMOVE denies, never add one, so it refuses no correct work.

R6. THE SEAM EXTENSION (option A, additive) AND THE CYCLE IT MUST NOT CREATE. Run-candidate resolution honouring R4 and R5 ships as a NEW EXPORT of scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, so the gate imports it rather than restating it, and it must distinguish a marker resolution from an inferred one, which today's bare-path return cannot express. THE IMPORT DIRECTION IS ALREADY TAKEN: plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs:71 imports activeIssueDir from validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, so a reverse edge for R5's literals closes a cycle. VERIFIED, on the real 16-module graph rather than a stand-in, with cwd pinned so the comparison is controlled: baseline `node gate-phase-entry.mjs` exits 0 with 121 bytes of stdout and EMPTY stderr; with the reverse edge added it exits 1 with 0 bytes of stdout and 808 bytes of stderr reading `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'IN_FLIGHT_MS' before initialization`; entered from the validator instead, the identical cycle is invisible. gate-phase-entry.mjs's try/catch wraps main(), not module evaluation, and its own comment says stderr there is read as a refusal, so the cycle converts a fail-open tooling gap into a phase REFUSAL. THE PREDICATE THEREFORE LIVES IN A LEAF MODULE that imports from neither participant, and both files import from it; this is stated here so the implementer is not left choosing between a cycle, an unnamed third module, and the private copy R16 forbids. The leaf must expose the in-flight answer and the DATABILITY answer as SEPARATE observations, because R5 gives the two consumers deliberately opposite answers for an undatable record and neither may re-derive the other's. VERIFIED that this closes it: with the leaf in place the same pinned-cwd run exits 0 with stderr empty and stdout BYTE-IDENTICAL to baseline, and a cycle detector over scripts/*.mjs reports 0 cycles at 17 modules where the reverse-edge tree reported 1 (`gate-phase-entry.mjs -> validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs -> gate-phase-entry.mjs`) and exited 1.

R7. FORBIDDEN SET DECIDED BY WHAT IS STAGED, NOT BY TEXT, AND NOT BY AN ELEVEN-ROW LITERAL TABLE. The gate must refuse invocations that stage paths the caller did not name. A decision taken by searching the raw command string denies correct work whose text merely MENTIONS a banned spelling - this issue's own ten-file doc retirement produces exactly that commit. A decision taken by matching whole literal spellings under-refuses everything nobody enumerated: VERIFIED with real git that `git commit -aqm 'm'` commits every tracked modification (1 file changed) while matching none of the enumerated rows, because git bundles short flags. The matching must therefore be specified over FLAG SEMANTICS - a staging verb (`add`/`stage`/`commit`) carrying an all-tracked flag (`-a`, `-A`, `-u`, or their long forms) in any bundled or separated spelling, or a blanket pathspec (`.`, `:/`), with no pathspec that narrows it - rather than over a list of strings. The enumerated rows are FIXTURES OF THAT CLASS, not the rule, and R7's floor clause is checked in the direction that catches a literal table (AC7's combined-flag rows). `git add -u` is the #19 harm exactly - git's man page: 'If no <pathspec> is given when -u option is used, all tracked files in the entire working tree are updated' - and a neighbour's planted mutation lives in a tracked file. Each spelling is also reachable under `cd x && `, `git -C <path>` and `git -c k=v`. TWO POPULATIONS THE ROUND-5 SPEC DID NOT CARRY, both found by QA and both failing in opposite directions. (i) THE STAGING-VERB TERM HAS NO NEGATIVE POPULATION: `git checkout`, `git restore`, `git stash`, `git clean`, `git diff` and `git log` appear nowhere in the spec as NOT-denied, so a mutation widening the deny to any `git` invocation passes every fixture. That mutation would refuse `git checkout -- .`, which agents/qa.md rule 13 mandates BY NAME for restoring a planted mutation from git, so the gate would break the very battery discipline it exists to protect. (ii) A COMPOUND COMMAND CAN STAGE NARROWLY AND THEN COMMIT BLANKET: `git add <path> && git commit -a` must be DENIED. Two plausible implementations get it wrong in the permissive direction - 'decide on the first git invocation' sees an explicit-path add, and 'any pathspec present -> allow' sees a pathspec - so the rule is that EVERY git invocation in a compound command is evaluated, and a deny by any one of them denies the whole call.

R8. Explicit-path staging must not be denied, whatever path is staged, including paths under .pipeline, and including a pathspec given to a flag that would otherwise be blanket (`git add -u <path>`). A gate that denies by inspecting WHICH path was staged does not satisfy this.

R9. TREE-AGNOSTIC. A Phase 4 subagent must not blanket-stage in ANY tree, including its own isolated one (staging a planted mutation is the #19 harm one layer in). This removes the need to identify the shared dispatch worktree from a payload whose cwd is the process-global cwd, not the caller's.

R10. TWO-STAGE BY DESIGN, STATED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED. All three Phase 2 reviewers independently found the same contradiction: R6's module reuse costs a node process (66.68 ms/call recorded) against a ceiling of 3x a 4.45 ms bash baseline. The gate must conclude 'not a candidate' without starting node and escalate only on the narrow plausible-deny branch. Stated as a requirement because the alternative reconciliations are both bad: blowing the bound, or privately re-deriving resolution in shell. ROUND 8 CORRECTS THE CEILING THIS REQUIREMENT CITES WITHOUT CHANGING WHAT IT REQUIRES: the 3x-of-baseline ceiling in its ABSOLUTE form sits below the test harness's own per-call floor - a do-nothing stub measures 25-28 ms/call through that harness against a 24-27 ms/call bound - so it is retired by AC18 in favour of a bound on the gate's MARGINAL cost over that stub on the identical path. The design obligation here is unchanged and is proven structurally by AC16's fork count; only the ceiling's methodology moved.

R11. ONE VOCABULARY, TWO STAGES. Both stages derive the forbidden set and the Phase 4 phase literals from ONE source. Two independently maintained lists do not satisfy this even if they agree the day they ship: a spelling the cheap stage misses is never denied and no criterion reddens.

R12. PHASE LITERALS FROM THEIR WRITER, AND AN ATTRIBUTION THAT IS ACTUALLY READ. plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md writes '4-review', '4-review-complete' and '4-veto-rework-required'; tests/test-status-schema-contract.sh already holds that vocabulary in both-directions set equality against it. The gate must not add a third private spelling. Separately, the gate records a role attribution derived from agent_type via the shared namespace strip, which is what makes R2's agent_type half enforceable rather than decorative. ALL THREE LITERALS MUST BE ASSERTED BEHAVIOURALLY, not merely held in a vocabulary set. AC15 pins the vocabulary; it does not pin a verdict, so only '4-review' was ever exercised end to end. The other two fall on opposite sides of the harm and `phase === '4-review'` and `phase.startsWith('4-')` diverge on both silently: '4-veto-rework-required' is a LIVE phase where rework subagents are actively dispatched, so an equality implementation leaves the gate silent exactly when panelist-driven rework is running; '4-review-complete' is a parked phase where a deny is comparatively cheap.

R13. DENY CHANNEL, BOUND TO ONE OBSERVATION. A deny travels as `hookSpecificOutput` with hookEventName 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision 'deny', permissionDecisionReason; the hook exits 0 in every case including a deny, so exit 2 is never used and the exit code cannot be confused with a verdict. Verified in 2.1.85: the consumer reads `H.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason||H.reason||"Blocked by hook"` and throws on a mismatched hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName. Assertions are taken on the parsed decision a caller receives, never on raw stdout, with the version recorded beside them.

R14. FAIL-OPEN, AND ATTRIBUTABLE. Every tooling gap and every abstention produces no deny. But which gap caused a non-action must be recoverable afterwards without re-running the session, and the gaps must be mutually distinguishable. HALVES: the attribution is available ON DEMAND and is NOT emitted unconditionally on the non-acting fast path, because a gate that writes on every Bash call of every adopting session is the permanent tax R10 exists to refuse.

R15. NO COMMAND STRINGS OUT, ACROSS EVERY SURFACE INCLUDING THE STAGE HANDOFF. No output or artifact the gate produces may carry the caller's command string or any substring other than the matched forbidden token. The enumerated sinks are: stdout, stderr, any file created or appended under any resolved root or temp dir, AND the argument vector and environment of any child process the gate spawns - the fourth arrived with R10's split and is readable by other local users on an adopting host. The escalation does not need the command string: R11 puts the table in one source and AC17 asserts the two stages agree, so the match is decided before the seam is reached. Project authority: plugins/pipeline/agents/secops.md:125, 'Never log secrets, tokens, or PII beyond request IDs. User-controlled text is sanitized before logging.'

R16. NO SECOND DERIVATION ON THE ESCALATION PATH. Active-issue resolution, run-candidate resolution, the in-flight/datability predicate and agent-identity parsing come from shared exports - validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's activeIssueDir, ISSUE_DIR_RE, R6's new export and the namespace strip promoted to a shared export, plus R6's leaf module for the predicate - never private copies. ISSUE_DIR_RE's own comment records what a second copy cost: voice-lint.mjs carried a private /^\d+$/ and exp- runs stayed invisible to it. R10's fast reject stage is exempt by construction and R11 pins its narrowness.

R17. DISARM, OPERATOR-ONLY, ACROSS EVERY CHANNEL, AND TRACEABLE. Ship a documented disarm following the existing CLAUDE_HOOK_*_SKIP naming convention. WHERE THE CITATION ACTUALLY LANDS, corrected: plugins/pipeline/hooks/stop.sh:64 is the skip line covering the ADVISORY half only, and :60-63 immediately above it carve halting controls OUT of that convention in terms this requirement must answer rather than cite past - 'an environment variable that disarms a halting control leaves no trace in the archived run record, and this repo has already refused that shape twice' - as does plugins/pipeline/README.md:84. THIS GATE SITS OUTSIDE THAT CARVE-OUT, and the reason is stated so nobody re-litigates it: the carve-out governs HALTING controls, and the phase-entry guard it protects is deliberately fail-CLOSED and un-disarmable, whereas this gate is a ratchet that fails OPEN by construction (R14) on every tooling gap and every abstention. But the carve-out's REASON - a suppression that leaves no trace - binds regardless of which side of it the gate sits on, so operating the disarm must produce its own non-action attribution, distinct from every one AC20 enumerates. SCOPE: the disarm must not be settable by the denied agent using only that agent's own tools in one tool call. Classes to enumerate: file writes under any resolved root, pipeline.config.json, and THE HOOK'S OWN INVOCATION ENVIRONMENT - the shell that runs the hooks.json command and whichever startup files it reads non-interactively, which on a zsh host includes ~/.zshenv; which files those are is an observation the suite makes and records. CHANNEL: the disarm's literal name must be absent from EVERY value-carrying field of the gate's emitted object, bound as a whole-stdout-and-stderr observation rather than per key. HALVES, and the cheap half stands: the operator README carries the disarm in FULL; a fix that satisfies the channel property by deleting it from the README does not satisfy this.

R18. PORTABILITY. The gate must resolve when the subagent's cwd has no .pipeline - an adopting project that gitignores it, which this repo's own .gitignore advises, leaves a Phase 4 dispatch worktree with none. R4's ownership property binds across every root consulted: resolving correctly in one root and letting a second root's newer record override it does not satisfy R4.

R19. HERMETIC VERIFICATION ONLY. A new hook takes effect only after publish -> marketplace refresh -> plugin update -> restart, so it cannot be exercised live in the session that builds it (#100/#66). Drive the hook script directly with payloads on stdin against a throwaway repo, the pattern tests/test-subagent-stop-hook.sh and tests/harness.sh:make_repo establish.

R20. CITE A PATH A READER CAN OPEN. Two different files in this repo are called README.md (the root, 39 lines, and plugins/pipeline/README.md, which carries the in-flight definition, the CLAUDE_HOOK_*_SKIP convention and the opt-out-knob ruling at line 84). Every citation in the shipped artifacts and comments must carry the path, so following it reaches the literal rather than the wrong file's EOF.

R21. DOC RETIREMENT, WITH ALL SIX RESIDUALS IN IT, IN ALL TEN FILES. Retire 'nothing mechanically enforces it either' in all ten files. PRECISION, because three readers got this wrong during #19 itself: the replacement goes in all TEN files, but byte-identity is required and asserted only across the NINE agents/*.md copies; plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:812 carries a compressed, non-identical restatement and stays that way. COMPRESSION IS WORDING, NOT CONTENT: the compressed copy carries ALL the residuals, so every per-clause file count is ten. That is ruled rather than left open because residual (a)'s audience is the orchestrator and plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md is the file the orchestrator reads. The residuals: (a) the orchestrator's own blanket commit, which R2's agent_id term exempts by design while the retired sentence says 'yours or the orchestrator's'; (b) a REQUEST_CHANGES fix round, which loops to the Dev step at current_phase '3-impl'; (c) THE ABSTENTION, WHOSE TWO BRANCHES HAVE DIFFERENT REMEDIES AND MUST BE STATED SEPARATELY - a single sentence attaching one remedy to both is false for one of them. BRANCH (c1), TWO OR MORE in-flight records and no honoured marker: the gate enforces nothing, and this IS closable by propagating an explicit active-issue signal (#111), because a marker naming one of the candidates resolves it under R4(3). BRANCH (c2), ZERO in-flight records: the gate enforces nothing, and this is NOT closable by the marker, by construction - R25(a) honours a marker only when the record it names is itself in-flight, and a zero-candidate root has no such record, so no marker can ever lift this branch out of abstention. #110's stale-final_verdict scenario is one way to reach (c2). The shipped sentence must name both branches and attach the remedy only to (c1); (d) R3's over-refusal, that a non-panelist subagent's blanket staging is denied while a Phase 4 run is the resolved owner; (e) THE DENY IS SUPPRESSIBLE BY ENLARGING THE CANDIDATE SET - one plain Write of a valid-JSON status.json with no parseable updated_at under a resolved root creates a second candidate and abstains the gate, in one tool call, through a directory panelists write to as routine work. (e) is disclosure, not a fix requirement: it is attributed under AC20 rather than silent, and closing it would require refusing the shard writes AC8 exists to permit. (f) A DELTA ROUND CARRYING A STALE final_verdict IS EXCLUDED FROM THE CANDIDATE SET, so the gate abstains on a genuinely live Phase 4 run whose record still carries the prior round's verdict - proven on this repo's own history and tracked as #110, which this issue does not fix. Omitting any of the six ships a claim-MORE defect in the artifact this issue exists to make honest.

R22. STALE-CLAIM SYNC. Update every consumer of the 'three hooks' fact: plugins/pipeline/README.md:142 (the literal count), plugins/pipeline/README.md:148 (the 'drives each hook end to end' coverage claim), README.md:24 at the repository root (the tree listing), and plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:95, whose dependency note already warns that a commit-triggered hook must not match a status-only checkpoint's path filter and must now name this hook.

R23. DO NOT READ review_rounds for any decision. It is optional, hand-maintained, and this repo's own telemetry schema records it disagreeing with the events it summarizes on 5 of 7 committed records in both directions. Any predicate needing 'has this run been through the panel' reads events[].

R24. NO MECHANICAL DIGEST EXISTS TODAY for either replicated span, so AC29's byte-identity assertion is new test surface this issue's own suite adds rather than something already wired. Do not assume an existing check will catch a drifted copy.

R25. THE MARKER PATH: WIDEN-ONLY, ADOPTING THIS REPO'S SHIPPED RULING RATHER THAN DEPARTING FROM IT. THIS REVERSES ROUND 4's R25, which ruled the marker deny-reducing-only. That ruling was wrong in two independent ways and both reviewers found one each, pointing the same direction. (1) It made setting `CLAUDE_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE` or `PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE` functionally identical to operating R17's disarm - the gate simply stops refusing - while R17's disarm gets class-by-class reachability testing (AC23) and the marker got none. 'The reachable outcome is fewer refusals rather than more' is inverted reasoning for a control whose entire function is to refuse: fewer refusals IS the disarm, and #19 rated the outcome it permits HIGH. (2) It foreclosed the only remedy this spec names for its own live residual: R21(c) discloses the concurrency abstention as the state a reader hits on arrival, q5's INVEST option routes the fix to propagating this very signal, and closing an abstention on a Phase 4 run means turning it into a DENY - which round-4 R25 forbade verbatim. A spec cannot disclose a residual, name one remedy, and forbid it. THE RULING, and it is this repo's existing decision rather than a new one: an explicit signal MUST NOT be able to NARROW the subject. plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs:30-33 states it - 'pointing it at a satisfied dir would be the env-var opt-out the design rejected, and it would leave no trace in the archived record. So both the signal-named dir and the mtime-derived dir are evaluated, and EITHER may refuse' - and :700-711 implements it, asking ONE resolver two questions via a `MTIME_ONLY` sentinel the issue-dir shape rejects, so the marker branch fails over to the mtime derivation without a second scan that could answer differently. R16 forbids a second derivation, so that mechanism is reused rather than restated. CONSEQUENCES, all three horns closed: the marker cannot suppress a deny, so it is not an off-switch and a denied agent that reaches it gains nothing; the marker CAN turn an abstention into a deny, which is exactly what q5's INVEST fallback needs and what keeps R21(c) coherent; and the precedent is adopted and cited rather than silently contradicted. TWO SUB-RULES BOUND THE COST. (a) The marker is honoured only when the record it names is itself in-flight per R5, so a stale marker pointing at a concluded or ancient run cannot manufacture denies forever - this too is already shipped and tested here (plugins/pipeline/tests/test-voice-lint.sh:1075 pins a staleness predicate applied on BOTH branches, with 'apply the predicate only on the mtime-fallback branch and this flips' as its own mutation). (b) A deny whose subject came from the marker rather than from the inference carries its own distinct attribution, so an over-refusal is diagnosable in one look. COST, NAMED because a guardrail must say what correct work it refuses: none today. Zero files under plugins/ assign either variable outside tests/, so with the marker absent the inferred path rules and behaviour is unchanged; and in the intended deployment the marker names the run the orchestrator is actually running, which IS the caller's run, so 'either may refuse' reduces to 'the caller's run refuses'. The residual over-refusal is a stale or hostile marker, and there the widen direction means the reachable outcome is more refusals, which no attacker wants and which sub-rule (b) makes visible. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TESTABLE HERE, corrected in round 6 after SecOps's own case-split. Given R25(a) plus R4's resolution order, the union design and an override design produce the IDENTICAL verdict in every reachable state, so 'delete the widen-only constraint' is a theorem rather than a mutation and a control pinned on it can never fire. The enforceable term is the HONOURING PRECONDITION - whether the marker's record qualifies as in-flight under R5 - and AC38 is re-pinned there. The union/override equivalence is recorded in falsifiability_pass.unmutable with its reason rather than left as a control that quietly passes. ROUND 7 RAISES THE MARKER'S STANDING WITHOUT CHANGING ITS DIRECTION: under R4(3) an honoured marker is now the ONLY thing that can resolve ambiguity among two or more in-flight candidates, because the mtime derivation no longer may. That is still widen-only - the marker adds a resolvable subject where there was none and can never suppress a deny - and R25(a)'s honouring precondition still applies, so a marker naming a record outside the candidate set resolves nothing and the gate abstains.

AC18. COST, PARTITIONED, AND MEASURED AS A DIFFERENCE BECAUSE THE HARNESS IS THE FLOOR. ROUND 8 RETIRES THIS CRITERION'S ABSOLUTE 3x BOUND, and the reason is a measurement rather than a preference: driven through the suite's own `run_gate_raw` path, a DO-NOTHING stub (a file containing `exit 0`) costs 25-28 ms/call on darwin 25.5.0 / node v24.19.0 against a 3x-of-same-run-baseline bound of 24-27 ms/call, so an implementation that does nothing at all FAILS the bound, and on the rounds where such a stub came in under it, it did so on scheduling noise. The quantity the old bound measured was the harness's own per-call scaffolding - a subshell, an `env` exec, the hook, two output command substitutions and an `rm`, roughly 3.5x a bare `sh -c ':'` before the gate runs at all - so it was a threshold on a rendered measurement of the instrument (evidence.md rule 21). WHAT IS ASSERTED INSTEAD. In one round, with no other work between the figures and the same call count N (N >= 20) for every one of them, the suite measures three quantities: B, the same-run bash no-op baseline (`sh -c ':'`); S, the HARNESS FLOOR - the do-nothing stub driven through the IDENTICAL path by pointing the plugin-root substitution at a stub root, so the stub file sits where the hook sits and is reached by the same resolved command, and the stub carries NO SHEBANG and IS EXECUTABLE for the same reason the shipped hook does (a shebang buys the stub a second exec the gate does not pay, biasing the difference downward) and does NOT read stdin (so the difference charges the gate for its own payload read); and G, the per-call figure for each class. Subtracting S cancels the scaffolding and leaves the hook script's own body. THE BOUND IS ON THE DIFFERENCE: for each class decidable without the node seam, |G - S| <= 2 * B. THE 2 IS DERIVED, NOT PICKED - it is the whole multiple of B nearest the geometric midpoint of the measured pass and fail figures: marginal cost <= 4 ms observed over three rounds, ~85 ms with the mutation below, sqrt(4 * 85) = 18.4 ms, B = 8-9 ms, 18.4 / 8.7 = 2.1. BOTH DIRECTIONS OF THAT BOUND MEAN SOMETHING, which is why it is two-sided: over the bound is the gate doing process-scale work on the fast path; under it by more than one unit is the stub failing to be a floor, which VOIDS the measurement rather than passing it. The seam-requiring class's figure is RECORDED and never bounded, AND IT IS THIS CRITERION'S LIVE NON-ZERO CONTROL: (G_seam - S) > 2 * B must hold in the same run (observed 85-87 ms against a 16-18 ms bound), so every green transcript has watched this exact comparison report a violation, with nothing planted. Instrument controls, each asserted rather than printed: B > 0 and S > 0, or every difference is unfalsifiable; and S > B, which carries its own expiry - if the floor ever stops dominating, the scaffolding is no longer the dominant term and an absolute bound could be re-derived, so re-measure rather than assuming this ruling still holds. MUTATION: insert an unconditional node invocation on a no-seam class; its difference moves to roughly 85 ms, about 5x the bound, where under the old absolute form the mutation and the instrument were indistinguishable. THE DESIGN CLAIM ITSELF - no node process on the reject path - IS PROVEN BY AC16's FORK COUNT AND NOT BY THIS CRITERION; AC18 bounds the cost of the structure AC16 proves, and the two must not be read as two measurements of the same thing.

STALE-CLAIM SYNC. plugins/pipeline/README.md no longer says 'The three hooks', its end-to-end sentence names the new hook, the root README.md's hooks/ listing names it, and plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md's checkpoint dependency note (currently line 95) names this hook as the commit-triggered automation whose filter a widened checkpoint would newly match.

AC33. CITATIONS OPEN. For every 'README.md:<n>' reference in the shipped artifacts, comments and this spec, the named line of the NAMED PATH contains the literal attributed to it. The root README.md is 39 lines while the opt-out-knob ruling lives in the PLUGIN README, so a citation written as a bare README with no directory segment and a line number past 39 fails this. THAT COUNTER-EXAMPLE IS WRITTEN DESCRIPTIVELY ON PURPOSE, and it has now been broken a third time: a bulk citation-fix pass 'corrected' this very sentence into a VALID citation, which both destroys the illustration and leaves the criterion reading as though the correct form failed. The damage was invisible because the two copies of this artifact carried different versions of it. BOTH CITATION FAMILIES, not just README. The check covers EVERY `<path>:<n>` citation in the shipped artifacts, comments and this spec: the named line of the named path, resolved from the repository root, must contain the literal the requirement attributes to it. A citation whose path does not resolve at all is a failure, not a skip. THE CHECK MUST NOT TRIP ON ITS OWN COUNTER-EXAMPLES, and this is a real trap rather than a hypothetical: writing an illustrative BAD citation as a literal `path:line` makes it indistinguishable from a real one, so the check flags text whose whole purpose is to name the failing form. I hit it twice - once when a bulk path rewrite silently 'corrected' three deliberate bad-form mentions including this criterion's own mutation, and once when the surviving example made AC33 red against itself. Counter-examples are therefore written DESCRIPTIVELY, never as a parseable literal. Asserted by running the check over this spec and requiring zero failures, which is the same observation an implementer runs over the shipped artifacts. THE SPEC IS NOT PRESENT IN EVERY DEPLOYMENT, AND THE ABSENT BRANCH IS AN ASSERTION RATHER THAN EITHER A SKIP OR AN AUTOMATIC FAILURE (ROUND 8). This repo excludes every per-issue artifact except the checkpoint from git - the `.pipeline/*/*` line of its .gitignore, with a `!.pipeline/*/status.json` negation re-including only status.json - so the in-flight spec does not exist in a fresh clone and never will. MEASURED on a real `git clone --no-hardlinks` of this branch: the issue's own .pipeline directory is not present in the clone at all, `git check-ignore` reports the spec path ignored by that line, and all 12 tracked files under .pipeline are status.json (0 are not). The fresh-checkout case in the issue-17 integration suite runs this ENTIRE suite inside such a clone and requires every suite green, so a spec-scan row written to report absence as a FAILURE hard-fails every clone run by construction, independent of whether the gate is correct - a check about the deployment wearing a gate criterion's name. Reporting it as a silent skip is the opposite defect and is worse, because an absent corpus that passes is exactly the shape evidence.md's empty-population rule refuses. THE RULE, in two halves: the citation scan over the SHIPPED (git-tracked) artifacts is unconditional and must find a non-empty population, unchanged; the scan over the in-flight spec runs when the spec is present, and when it is absent the suite ASSERTS THE REASON - that the absence is explained by this repo's own exclusion, read from git rather than from a comment, namely that the path is reported ignored AND at least one file under .pipeline is tracked AND every tracked file under .pipeline is a status.json. An absence git cannot explain that way is still a FAILURE, which is the case the 'never a skip' clause was written for. The absent branch carries its own non-zero control, run in EVERY deployment including the one where the spec IS present, so the branch is never dead code in the tree that authored it: the same predicate applied to a scratch repository carrying no .pipeline exclusion rule must report the absence UNEXPLAINED. COMMITTING THE SPEC TO SATISFY THIS ROW IS REFUSED: it would make the check pass by changing the repo rather than the check, and it would retire the status.json-only checkpoint convention that this issue's own six review rounds and several other suites depend on.

AC38. MARKER PRECEDENCE, EVERY CELL ASSERTED, IN THE WIDEN DIRECTION. Build a root holding one in-flight record at '3-impl' and a second at '4-review'. Send a payload with agent_id present and a command from AC7; record the verdict. Then, ONE AT A TIME, set `input.active_issue`, `CLAUDE_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE` and `PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE` to name each dir in turn, replay the BYTE-IDENTICAL payload, and record verdict and attribution. Per R25: NO cell may go from deny to non-deny (the marker cannot suppress); a cell naming the '4-review' record MAY go from abstain to deny, and when it does the deny carries the marker-subject attribution R25(b) requires, distinct from an inference-subject deny. A marker naming a record R5 excludes (concluded, or stale) is NOT honoured and falls back to the inference, per R25(a). REACHABILITY, the half round 4 omitted entirely and the reason SecOps rated this high: for each class AC23 already enumerates - a file write under any resolved root, pipeline.config.json, and each observed non-interactive startup file of the shell that executes the hooks.json command - and for each of the two environment spellings, perform the one-tool-call set-step and replay the byte-identical denied payload; the deny must PERSIST in every cell. If it does not for some class, that is the finding and the marker's handling has to be re-ruled, the same escape AC23 carries for the disarm. Deleting the widen-only constraint must redden at least the cells where the marker names a record whose phase disagrees with the inferred one. RE-PINNED IN ROUND 6. The union/override control round 5 named cannot fire: given R25(a) and R4's resolution order the two designs produce identical verdicts in every reachable state, so that 'mutation' is a theorem and is recorded in falsifiability_pass.unmutable instead. THE TESTABLE TERM IS THE HONOURING PRECONDITION: a marker naming a record R5 EXCLUDES (concluded, then separately stale) must NOT be honoured and must fall back to the inference; deleting the precondition must redden exactly those cells. REACHABILITY CELLS MUST CHANGE A VERDICT, not restate the status quo: round 5's matrix asserted the deny persists in every cell, which passes identically whether the marker mechanism works, is a no-op, or the set-step never reached the hook at all. For EACH channel class, add one cell where that channel demonstrably CHANGES the outcome - set the marker through that class to name an in-flight record at a Phase 4 phase in a root that would otherwise abstain, and assert the verdict moves from abstain to DENY with the marker-subject attribution. A class whose verdict-changing cell does not fire has not been shown to reach the hook, and the persistence cells over it prove nothing. PRECONDITIONS ARE ASSERTED, AND A CELL WHOSE PRECONDITION FAILS IS VOID. Round 6's verdict-changing cell states no precondition on the root it runs against, and under every reading a reader would naturally take it cannot fire for any channel class - which is round 5's cannot-fire defect one level deeper, inside the criterion re-pinned to fix it. Each verdict-changing cell must ASSERT BOTH PREMISES BEFORE reading the verdict: (P1) with the marker UNSET the root abstains, and (P2) the record the marker names IS in R5's candidate set for that root, so R25(a) will honour it. Only then is the post-set verdict read, and it must be DENY. If P1 or P2 fails the cell is VOID - reported as not-run with the failing premise named, NOT as a pass, NOT as a failure, and NOT as 'the channel does not reach the hook', which is the misreading that turns a fixture-construction defect into a phantom mechanism defect. A run in which every cell is VOID must fail the suite, because a matrix that never fired has measured nothing.

AC41. THE RESOLVER'S ANSWER AND THE NARROWING MUST BE MADE TO DISAGREE, OR THE NARROWING IS UNTESTED. The shared resolver R16 mandates is in-flight-BLIND on both its paths: it consults directory names, status.json mtime and the marker, and never reads final_verdict or updated_at. Every fixture population elsewhere in this spec is built from in-flight dirs, so the resolver and R5's candidate set agree in every cell and a mutation DELETING THE NARROWING ENTIRELY would pass the whole suite. Required, and stated as the population rather than as a row: a root where the two actively disagree - one record at '3-impl' with a fresh parseable updated_at and no final_verdict, plus a second at '4-review' that R5 EXCLUDES (once by a stale updated_at, separately by a final_verdict) and that is the NEWEST by status.json mtime, so the raw resolver returns the excluded dir. Driven with agent_id present and a command from AC7, the outcome is NOT DENIED. Repeated for each of R25's three marker channels naming the excluded dir, which per R25(a) is not honoured either. DISCRIMINATION, TWO CELLS, because round 5 collapsed them and took the wrong branch - asserting DENY for a state R21(c), AC12(i), AC30(c) and AC38 all separately assert as ABSTAIN. CELL (i): re-date the excluded '4-review' record so it is in flight, leaving the '3-impl' record in place. The candidate set becomes TWO and the verdict stays NOT DENIED - but the ATTRIBUTION must change, from 'the resolver named a record the narrowing excludes' to the R4 ownership abstention. The verdict is identical in both states, so attribution is the only thing that can discriminate here, and a criterion that asserted the verdict alone would pass under either. CELL (ii): re-date that record AND remove the '3-impl' record, so the '4-review' record is the SOLE candidate; the verdict flips to DENIED. Only cell (ii) may assert a deny. THE MUTATION THIS EXISTS FOR: delete the narrowing and pass the resolver's raw answer straight through. ITS REDDENING SET IS NAMED, NOT CLAIMED TO BE ONE. Round 5 and round 6 both asserted 'AC41 reddens and no other criterion does', and DBA measured that the mutation reddens SIX criteria - the collateral grew when round 6 added AC42. A mutation that reddens six is not a defect in the mutation; asserting it reddens one is a defect in the spec. The suite therefore states the expected set IN ADVANCE and asserts equality with the observed set: AC41, AC12, AC30(c), AC38, AC40 and AC42 all depend on the narrowing and all must redden together, and any criterion outside that named set going red means the mutation reached something nobody predicted, which is itself the finding.

AC42. OWNERSHIP UNDER A REAL CLONE, AND THE TIE IS NOT THE VARIABLE. Round 6 built this criterion on an mtime TIE and that premise is false for the deployment it was written about. spec.size_justification: RULING, third statement, unchanged in direction: one issue, do not split. 27 requirements and 40 criteria against a 10/12 budget, a fourth statement of the same ruling. THE GROWTH IS ENTIRELY REVIEW-DRIVEN AND THE SCOPE STATEMENT HAS NEVER MOVED: one hook script, one predicate, one bash suite, one doc retirement, plus - new this round and the only scope change in three rounds - one additive export on an existing module, ruled in seam_extension_ruling and admitted explicitly in out_of_scope rather than discovered later. Of the criteria added since intake, every one traces to a named Phase 2 must_satisfy on the mechanism already specified, not to a new deliverable. THE COUNT IS DRIVEN BY DIRECTION PAIRS, and two rounds have now proved that is not theoretical: round 1 found the headline control (AC2) survived its own mutation, and round 2 found the whole allow-direction of the forbidden table unasserted, so a substring matcher would have passed every positive cell while denying this issue's own doc-retirement commits. Both were holes in the same shape - a table checked only in the direction that catches defects, never in the direction that refuses correct work. Eleven of thirty-five now exist only as twins: AC2/AC4, AC11's halves, AC7/AC8, AC9's mention/invoke pairs, AC12's (i)/(ii), AC13's touch-stability pair, AC21/AC24, AC22's four channels, AC23's two directions, AC27/AC28. Delete them and this reads as twenty-four and describes a gate nobody has watched refuse correct work. THE MATRICES ARE STILL NOT A COUNT DRIVER: AC7's 11x4, AC9's per-row pairing, AC10's 18, AC13's 8 and AC20's 9 sit INSIDE single criteria. COUPLING TIGHTENED AGAIN THIS ROUND. AC30/AC31 now bind the ten-file doc text to four fixture outcomes, so the doc edit and the mechanism cannot be verified apart at all; and AC27/AC28 bind the seam extension to proving it changed nothing else. Neither sequencing is available: docs-first ships ten files asserting an enforcement that does not exist; hook-first ships a live gate ten files say does not exist. THE SPLIT CANDIDATE HAS CHANGED AND IS NOW WEAKER, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING. At intake I named the namespace-strip extraction as the one honest boundary. It is now part of a larger seam extension (R6) that R4 depends on, so cutting it would leave the hook issue blocked on its own prerequisite rather than merely sequenced after it. There is no clean cut left; the honest answer is that this issue got bigger because two rounds of review found the mechanism needed more than it looked like, and the alternative to carrying that is shipping the smaller thing that does not work. ROUND-3 ADDENDUM: the five criteria added this round are AC36 (no cycle, both entry points equivalent), AC37 (an undatable record is never the resolved owner), AC38 (marker precedence), AC39 (the disarm is traceable) and AC40 (the disclosed suppression is the actual behaviour). Four of the five are direction twins of properties already present - AC37 is the unstated half of R5's own argument, AC38 the unstated half of the ruling's, AC39 the trace half of R17's scope half, AC40 the reachability half of R21(e)'s disclosure - which is the same pattern every round has produced and the reason the count is what it is. AC36 is the only genuinely new subject, and it exists because a reviewer found a real module cycle rather than a wording gap. Nothing was added that is not a must_satisfy on the mechanism already specified. ROUND-4 ADDENDUM: one criterion added (AC41), and it is the clearest example yet of why this spec is the size it is. AC41 is not a new subject; it is the discovery that every fixture population in the other forty criteria happens to sit in the cell where the shared resolver and the narrowing AGREE, so a mutation deleting the narrowing entirely would have passed the whole suite. That is a property of the POPULATION, not of any one row, which is exactly the class of gap QA is joining Phase 2 to audit. The rest of this round is corrections to existing text: a reversed ruling (R25), a fixed evaluation order (R5), a count that disagreed with itself in one place out of four (AC30), an arithmetic that could not close (AC31), reference literals that were measurements of the runner (AC36/measured_state), and two miscitations. None of it widens scope. ROUND-5 ADDENDUM: one criterion added (AC42, the mtime tie) and one residual added to the doc text (f, #110). Every other change is a population addition inside an existing criterion - a negative command set for R7's staging-verb term, two compound-command cells, two phase literals that were pinned by vocabulary but never by verdict, two abstention paths that were never checked as leakage sinks, and one verdict-CHANGING cell per marker channel class. That is precisely the lens QA was added for, and the result argues the lens was worth adding rather than that the spec grew: five of QA's six findings are empty complements - populations whose absence let a specific named mutation pass the entire suite - and none of them is a new deliverable. ROUND-6 ADDENDUM: no criterion added. R4 got SHORTER - three rounds of ordered rules with an exception collapsed into a three-branch prohibition - and AC12 and AC42 simplified with it, which is what a correct rule does to the workarounds that were compensating for a wrong one. Everything else this round is a correction: an honest reddening set for AC41's mutation, asserted preconditions for AC38, a per-branch remedy in R21(c), quote-aware splitting, and 20 citation paths that did not resolve from the repository root.

open_questions.question: Should this hook also block a Phase 4 panelist from editing a tracked file in the shared worktree (the Write/Edit half of the rule), or only the blanket git-staging half?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Under NARROW: 'a Write to a tracked path by a Phase 4 panelist is not denied' — a Bash-only ratchet. Under BROAD: 'a Write whose resolved path is tracked is denied unless it is the panelist's own shard' — a per-write git subprocess against R10's cost argument, plus an exemption whose correctness depends on a downstream .gitignore. Both Phase 2 rounds strengthened narrow: path-based discrimination is exactly where this design goes wrong (round 1's AC3/AC6 unsatisfiability), and AC8 now pins that a .pipeline path gets no special treatment.

options.label: Narrow (Bash blanket-staging only)
options.implication: Closes the cited sentence, no per-write subprocess, no wedge path.

options.label: Broad (also deny tracked Write/Edit)
options.implication: Closes both halves, at the cost of a failure mode that halts the panel rather than permitting a defect.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: Narrow. The broad half's worst case (a wedged Phase 4 in someone else's project) is worse than its best case; the narrow half has no such path.

open_questions.question: Should the gate deny blanket staging even inside the panelist's own correctly-isolated worktree?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Under YES the gate needs no notion of which tree it is looking at, which matters because the payload's cwd is the process-global cwd rather than the subagent's. Under NO the gate must answer a question the payload does not support and fails open whenever it cannot, making the bypass 'have isolated'.

options.label: Yes, tree-agnostic
options.implication: Simplest predicate; refuses staging a planted mutation in the isolated tree, the #19 harm one layer in.

options.label: No, only in the shared tree
options.implication: Closer to the wording, but depends on a tree identification the payload does not support.

open_questions.question: What form should the disarm take, and how is it documented?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Round 1's resolution ('named in the deny reason') was wrong: a deny sets blockingError from permissionDecisionReason, which the model reads. Round 2 found the fix bound on one of four channels that reach the denied agent. Both are now R17 properties rather than open choices; what remains open is the concrete form.

options.label: CLAUDE_HOOK_*_SKIP env var, README-documented
options.implication: Matches plugins/pipeline/hooks/stop.sh:64; an env var set outside the session is not settable by the denied agent in one tool call — subject to AC23's shell-startup-file observation, which could falsify that.

options.label: A marker file or a pipeline.config.json key
options.implication: Both writable by the denied agent with its own tools; fails R17's scope property outright.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: The env var following CLAUDE_HOOK_*_SKIP, documented in full in the README, absent from every output channel. The file and config forms are ruled out by R17's scope property. AC23's observation step exists because the env var's own safety depends on which startup files the hook's shell reads, which I have not measured.
open_questions.resolution: env var, CLAUDE_HOOK_*_SKIP convention; README full, every output channel silent; safety re-verified by AC23's observation

open_questions.question: Should the gate treat any current_phase beginning '4-' as in scope, or only an exact set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An exact set goes silently inert the first time a new slug appears; a prefix admits any future 4-*. Both produce a passing AC11.

options.label: Prefix on '4-'
options.implication: Cannot go inert on a new slug.

options.label: Exact enumerated set
options.implication: Precise today, stops firing quietly the day a slug is added — #66 in miniature.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: Prefix on '4-', with the three literals plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md actually writes asserted as fixtures, and R12/AC15 tying the vocabulary to its writer.
open_questions.resolution: prefix on '4-', vocabulary derived from plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md

open_questions.question: Is an abstaining gate acceptable as the shipped steady state, given that on this repo two records are in flight and the gate abstains on every call?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Under ACCEPT: AC13 stands, the gate acts only on an unambiguous single in-flight run, and a two-run host gets no enforcement until one run concludes. Under INVEST: the orchestrator propagates an explicit active-issue signal, which touches plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md's dispatch convention inside this issue. ROUND 4 CHANGED THIS QUESTION'S STANDING: R25's reversal means the marker CAN close the abstention, so INVEST is a live path rather than a forbidden one, and R21(c)'s shipped sentence must name it as the remedy.

options.label: Accept abstention
options.implication: Ships now, no orchestrator change; on a two-run host the gate enforces nothing and says so only through AC20's attribution and R21(c)'s sentence.

options.label: Invest in the explicit signal
options.implication: Works under concurrency, at the cost of widening the diff into the dispatch convention while the gate is unproven in deployment. SecOps measured the receiving half as already built and self-tested; the outstanding work is propagation only, so this is cheaper than I first stated but still real.

open_questions.ba_recommendation: Accept, and SecOps independently ruled the same way on the mechanism. Abstention refuses no correct work, it is the fail-open direction the whole design takes, and it is reversible. What was NOT acceptable — and is now fixed as R21(c)/AC30(c)/AC31 rather than left to a summary — is shipping the abstention underneath a replacement sentence that names only two residuals. A control that is sometimes inert and never wrong beats a comment; a control that is inert while nine agent contracts say it is enforced is worse than the comment it replaced. UNCHANGED AFTER THE REVERSAL, and worth saying why: R25 now permits the marker to close the abstention, but permitting is not propagating. The orchestrator still has to set the signal, which touches the dispatch convention, and that stays out of scope here. What changed is that the residual sentence can now honestly name a remedy instead of disclosing a dead end.
open_questions.resolution: accept the abstention; the concurrency residual is named in the replacement text TOGETHER WITH its remedy, which R25's widen-only ruling makes real

spec.ba_notes: Round-6 rework, in stride rather than a full round. THE STRUCTURAL FIX IS THAT R4 IS NOW A PROHIBITION, NOT AN ORDER WITH AN EXCEPTION, and the coordinator is right that rounds 4, 5 and 6 each reintroduced newest-mtime-decides-ownership in a new costume - selector, then tie-break, then 'select AMONG them, never outside them', whose only bound was the outside. The rule: narrow by R5; zero candidates abstain; exactly one is the owner; two or more are resolved ONLY by an honoured marker naming one of that set, and otherwise abstain unconditionally with no tie-break and no distinction between a tied and an untied mtime, because mtime is not consulted in that branch at all. The mtime derivation now has no role in ownership in any branch. I VERIFIED BOTH REPRO CASES AGAINST A REAL CLONE RATHER THAN A SYNTHETIC ROOT, and QA's warning was exactly right and changed the answer. A real `git clone --no-hardlinks` of this repo puts all 12 tracked status.json files in ONE whole second - `stat -f %m` reports the same value for every one - while node's mtimeMs carries sub-millisecond decimals and all 12 are DISTINCT, so the resolver finds a strict winner and NO TIE OCCURS. My round-6 AC42 was built on a tie that a clone does not produce, and a `touch -t` fixture would have 'passed' while testing a state that never happens. What actually decides the clone case is the candidate COUNT: that clone carries TWO in-flight records (98 at '4-review', and 106), so under round 6's clause (4) the newest in-flight candidate would have owned the deny and refused correct work in 106's own session, on a fresh clone of this very repository - DBA's blocker reproduced without my having to construct it. Under the new rule the same root abstains. A third thing fell out of the same run and is worth recording: activeIssueDir on that clone returns exp-script-test-coverage, a record carrying a final_verdict that R5 excludes outright, so the clone exercises AC41's resolver-disagrees-with-narrowing shape naturally. AC42 is rebuilt on the real clone with a control that asserts the mtimeMs are distinct while the whole seconds are equal, so a future fixture cannot quietly go back to checking seconds and calling it a tie. ALSO FIXED: AC41's mutation reddens six criteria and the spec claimed one, twice - the honest fix is to name the expected set in advance and assert equality with the observed set, since a mutation reddening six is fine and asserting it reddens one is not; AC38's verdict-changing cells now assert BOTH premises before reading a verdict and are VOID rather than passing or failing when a premise fails, because round 6 let a fixture-construction defect read as a phantom mechanism defect; R21(c) now states its two branches separately, because #111's marker remedy provably closes only the two-or-more branch and can never close the zero-in-flight branch, where R25(a) has no in-flight record to honour; AC7 gains quote-aware splitting, whose fixture is this issue's own doc-retirement commit message; and 20 citations written without the plugins/pipeline prefix did not resolve from the repository root, now corrected to `plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:<n>` with AC33 widened from the README family to every path:line citation. CITATION FIX (in stride, non-blocking, after QA found AC33 red against the spec itself while authoring Phase 3a tests): 12 occurrences across 10 distinct citations did not resolve from the repository root - the same class as round 7s commands/pipeline.md fix, missed on the citations that did not match that one pattern. I fixed them by RUNNING AC33s own check rather than patching by hand, then verified each corrected path actually lands on the literal it is cited for (all eight targets confirmed by sed). The spec now passes its own criterion: 16 distinct citations, 24 occurrences, zero failures. TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING FROM IT. (1) The root README line count is retired from R20 rather than corrected. QA reported 40 where round 6 recorded 39, and BOTH are right under different grains - wc -l counts newlines and gives 39, splitting on newline counts the trailing empty element and gives 40. A number with two defensible grains that disagree by one, pinned in prose nothing re-derives, is exactly the shape this spec keeps refusing elsewhere; AC33s mechanical check carries the claim now, and any count stated anywhere must name the command that produced it. (2) AC33 gains a self-referential rule, because I hit the same trap twice: an illustrative BAD citation written as a literal path:line is indistinguishable from a real one, so a bulk rewrite silently corrected three deliberate counter-examples last round including AC33s own mutation, and the survivor then made AC33 red against itself. Counter-examples are now written descriptively, and the criterion is asserted by running the check over this spec and requiring zero failures. ROUND 8 (scoped ruling, AC18 and AC33 only): AC18's absolute 3x ratio is retired and replaced by a bound on the gate's MARGINAL cost over a do-nothing stub driven through the identical harness path, because the harness's own floor (25-28 ms/call) sits at or above the old bound (24-27 ms/call) and an empty implementation failed it; AC33's spec-scan row now asserts the REASON for an absent spec rather than reporting absence as a failure, because this repo's own .gitignore excludes every per-issue artifact but status.json and the fresh-clone integration case runs the whole suite inside a clone. RECONCILED AT THE SAME TIME: the two copies of this artifact had drifted - the worktree copy predated the round-7 citation fix, and the marketplace copy had had AC33's deliberate bad-form counter-example bulk-rewritten into a valid citation. Both copies are now byte-identical and the counter-example is descriptive.

concerns.description: ROUND 6's NEW R4 CLAUSE (4) RE-LICENSES THE MTIME-NEWEST OWNERSHIP DERIVATION THAT R4's OWN FIRST SENTENCE FORBIDS, AND IT CONTRADICTS FOUR CRITERIA INCLUDING THE ONE ROUND 6 REWROTE TO CLOSE MY ROUND-5 BLOCKER. R4 opens: ownership 'must never be decided by which unrelated concurrent or abandoned run wrote a status.json most recently.' Its new round-6 order then says: '(4) Two or more -> the marker (R25) and the mtime scan may select AMONG THEM, never outside them, and a tie there with no marker -> abstain.' The 'never outside them' bound is the only bound; a NON-tie with two in-flight candidates therefore resolves to the newest-mtime one and DENIES. REPRODUCED against the real module at origin/main ce7961e, in a pinned worktree, on AC12(i)'s exact fixture (two in-flight dirs, the OTHER one newer and reading '4-review', caller belongs to the 3-impl run): narrowing -> ['106','98']; activeIssueDir -> 98; R4(4) selects 98 (among the set); 98.current_phase = '4-review'; verdict DENIED. AC12(i) asserts NOT DENIED and names 'resolve from the newest-mtime dir regardless of ownership' as the mutation that must redden it - so the spec's requirement now IS its own criterion's named mutation. Same fixture, same contradiction, at AC41 cell (i) (re-dated record, both present, 'the verdict stays NOT DENIED'), AC30(c) (the two-in-flight residual fixture, abstain) and AC38's baseline (the '3-impl' + '4-review' root whose recorded verdict a marker 'MAY go from abstain to deny'). My harness discriminates rather than merely firing: eight other cells PASS against the spec's own predictions (AC42 i/ii/iii/iv, the origin/main-as-fresh-clone shape, the #110 shape, AC41 base and cell (ii)) and only this one diverges. THIS IS NOT ROUND 5's DEFECT RESTATED - it is its mirror image, introduced by the remediation. Round 5 had AC41 asserting DENY against four places asserting ABSTAIN; round 6 fixed AC41 and moved the DENY into R4 itself, so my round-5 must_satisfy ('no two criteria in this spec may assert different outcomes for the same root and payload') is still unmet. Round-5 R21(c) read 'the gate enforces nothing while more than one run is in flight and no marker names the active one', which was consistent; round-6 R21(c) reads 'when TWO OR MORE are and neither a marker nor the MTIME SCAN discriminates among them', which carries the same new licence into the sentence R21 requires shipped in all ten files. DIRECTION: claim-MORE. It refuses correct work, on the live shape - measured_state row 6 records TWO in-flight records as this repo's own state, and R21(c) calls that 'the live state of this repo today'. Concretely: run A at '3-impl' and run B at '4-review' both in flight, B's checkpoint written most recently (the normal case, because the active panel writes checkpoints), and run A's dev subagent running `git commit -a -m "feat: implement"` is DENIED on run B's phase. That is exactly the harm R4's first sentence exists to prevent. A charitable reading in which only the MARKER may select among two or more is available, and that reading is itself the defect: the two readings differ in the deny direction and the requirement does not say which, which is the identical failure mode round 4 found in R5's evaluation order and BA fixed by fixing the order.
concerns.must_satisfy: For a root holding two or more in-flight candidates with no marker set on any of R25's three channels, R4 and every criterion that constructs that root must state ONE verdict, and a reader who opens R4, R21(c), AC12(i), AC30(c), AC38's baseline and AC41 cell (i) must find the same answer in all six. Checked by: build AC12(i)'s fixture (two dirs, both no final_verdict and both with a fresh parseable updated_at, one at '3-impl' and one at '4-review', the '4-review' dir strictly NEWEST by status.json mtime, no marker, agent_id present, a command from AC7's table) and evaluate it against R4's resolution order and against AC12(i)'s assertion in the same suite; both must be satisfiable simultaneously, which they are not as written. If the ruling is that two-or-more with no marker ABSTAINS - which is what the four criteria say and what R4's first sentence requires - then R4 clause (4) must say the mtime scan may NOT select among candidates and only the marker may, and R21(c)'s shipped sentence must drop 'nor the mtime scan discriminates among them'. If the ruling is instead that the mtime scan may select among candidates, then R4's opening prohibition must be restated to permit it, AC12(i) must be re-pinned with a NEW mutation (its current one becomes a theorem, per the falsifiability_pass.unmutable discipline this spec already applies to AC38), and R21 must carry a SEVENTH residual naming the correct work refused: a subagent in a Phase 3 run denied on a concurrent Phase 4 run's phase, whenever the Phase 4 run's status.json is the newer file. Either way, a mutation that flips the two-or-more-no-marker branch between abstain and deny must redden a test named in advance.
concerns.location: spec.json R4 (RESOLUTION ORDER clause 4) against R4's opening sentence, R21(c), AC12(i), AC30(c), AC38 baseline, AC41 cell (i)

concerns.description: AC41'S NAMED MUTATION STILL CLAIMS IT REDDENS ALONE, AND ROUND 6 MADE THE CLAIM WORSE BY ADDING AC42. Carried unchanged from my round-5 major, and escalated because the collateral set GREW as a direct result of this round's remediation. AC41 ends, verbatim in both the criterion and falsifiability_pass: 'delete the narrowing and pass the resolver's raw answer through; AC41 must redden while every other criterion stays green' / 'AC41 reddens and no other criterion does.' MEASURED against the real activeIssueDir at origin/main ce7961e, in a pinned worktree: (i) AC12(i)'s root - raw resolver returns '98' at '4-review' where AC12(i) asserts NOT denied, so AC12(i) reddens, and AC12 says so itself ('a mutation resolving from the newest-mtime dir regardless of ownership must redden (i)'). (ii) AC42(i) - two dirs tied at one mtime, one in-flight at '4-review', one concluded: activeIssueDir -> null, so the raw answer yields no owner and no deny, while AC42(i) asserts IS DENIED; it reddens. (iii) AC42(iv), the fresh-clone shape, all four status.json forced to one tick: activeIssueDir -> null, raw answer no deny, AC42(iv) asserts IS DENIED; it reddens. (iv) AC37's three cells hold ONE undatable record at '4-review' and assert NOT denied; with no narrowing the raw resolver returns that sole dir and the gate denies, so all three redden. (v) AC13's evaluation-order discrimination cell cannot flip at all once the candidate-set size is no longer computed. So the observed set is at least six criteria against a stated expectation of one, and two of the six (AC42 i and iv) were introduced by THIS round's tie fix while AC41's sentence was left untouched. The harm is the spec's own tell turned against it: AC31 teaches that a mismatched count is the sign of a derived expectation, so an implementer who runs AC41's mutation and sees six red concludes the harness is wrong and relaxes AC41 - and AC41 is the only criterion that makes R5's narrowing observable at all ('a mutation DELETING THE NARROWING ENTIRELY would pass the whole suite' is AC41's own premise). Round 4 raised this exact defect against AC31 and BA closed it by naming both reddening tests; AC31 still carries that fix while AC41 does not.
concerns.must_satisfy: The set of criteria AC41's named mutation reddens must be stated BY IDENTIFIER in advance and must equal the set observed when the mutation is applied. Checked by: replace the candidate derivation with the resolver's bare return, run the full suite, record which criteria go red by identifier, and compare to AC41's list; 'every other criterion stays green' does not satisfy this while AC12(i), AC37, AC13's order cell and AC42(i)/(iv) are in the suite, and neither does a bare count. Each listed criterion's failure message must name the deleted narrowing rather than report a numeric mismatch, so a reader who did not write the battery can separate the intended catch from the collateral ones. If instead AC41 is meant to be the SOLE catcher, its fixture population must be one no other criterion shares, and the criterion must say which distinguishing property makes that true.
concerns.location: spec.json AC41 (final clause) and falsifiability_pass.one_mutation_per_criterion[AC41], against AC12(i), AC13 (evaluation-order cell), AC37, AC42(i), AC42(iv)

concerns.description: AC36(b)'s RECORD-STORE STATE IS STILL UNPINNED AND R26 STILL CARRIES THE FALSE 'EMPTY STDERR' PREMISE. Carried unchanged from round 5; nothing in the round-6 diff touches either. AC36(b) requires a paired same-run capture from the same cwd against the same record-store state and correctly forbids asserting against a literal byte count or against 'stderr is empty' - but it still never says that state must be one where gate-phase-entry actually DOES something. Pin cwd to an empty root and both sides produce exit 0 / 0 B / 0 B, the equality holds trivially, and AC36(b) degrades to an import-crash probe that AC36(a) already covers. The FUNCTION-scope cycle variant AC36(a)'s own text credits me with (cycle present, every runtime check clean) is precisely what then walks through, because (b) is the half that would otherwise be load-bearing on the behaviour. R26 actively steers the implementer there: it still reads 'the same exit code, the same stdout and the same empty stderr as at the reviewed commit'. A reader who opens R26, runs the command and gets non-empty stderr has been handed a false fact about the reviewed commit, and the cheapest way to make R26's sentence true is to run it from a root where the guard does nothing.
concerns.must_satisfy: AC36(b)'s paired capture must be taken against a record store in which the command under test exercises its REFUSING path, not merely its not-applicable path, and the fixture must prove it did. Checked by: on the baseline side of the same capture, assert a NON-EMPTY stderr and the exit code the guard uses for a refusal, before comparing the two sides - that is the non-zero control for the comparison itself, and a run whose baseline is exit 0 with empty output does not satisfy this because it cannot distinguish 'the entry points agree' from 'neither entry point reached the guard'. Repeat for each of the three entry directions AC36(b) names. Separately, R26's 'the same empty stderr' must be restated so it asserts equality between the two runs rather than a fact about the reviewed commit's output, since that output is a function of the .pipeline record store under cwd.
