It is not always', names the c337579 counterexample, names the direction as claim-LESS, and R21 goes to SIX residuals with (f) naming the delta-round exclusion; AC30(f), AC29 and AC31 all count six consistently. #110 is filed and states the finding correctly on substance (see the nit for the one figure it adds that I did not produce). VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY RATHER THAN ACCEPTED FROM THE REWORK NOTE. vulnerabilities.description: AC38's round-6 verdict-changing reachability cell states no precondition on the root it is run against, and BOTH readings a reader would naturally take make the cell unfireable for EVERY channel class - which is round 5's control-cannot-fire defect re-introduced one level down, inside the very criterion re-pinned to fix it. Measured against the pinned resolver at origin/main ce7961e (probe output quoted in the reply): (C5) on the obvious 'root that would otherwise abstain', i.e. ZERO in-flight records, the marker names a record R5 excludes, R25(a) refuses to honour it, and the verdict stays ABSTAIN - the cell cannot fire through any channel; (C7) on AC38's OWN declared base root ('one in-flight record at 3-impl and a second at 4-review', distinct mtimes) the gate does not abstain at all - it resolves to 107@3-impl under R4(4) - so that root cannot host an abstain->deny cell either. Only a root with two or more in-flight candidates that the mtime scan cannot separate fires it (C6: baseline ABSTAIN -> marker -> DENY with marker-subject attribution). The consequence is worse than a dead control, because AC38 attaches an escape to it: 'a class whose verdict-changing cell does not fire has not been shown to reach the hook, and the persistence cells over it prove nothing'. A fixture defect would therefore be read as a mechanism defect for all channel classes simultaneously, and AC38 instructs the implementer to re-rule the marker's handling on that reading - reversing R25 a third time on false evidence.
vulnerabilities.location: spec.json acceptance_criteria AC38 ('REACHABILITY CELLS MUST CHANGE A VERDICT'), against requirements R4(3)/R4(4) and R25(a)
vulnerabilities.remediation: The verdict-changing cell must carry BOTH of its premises as asserted steps taken BEFORE the verdict is read, and must be VOID rather than FAILING when either premise does not hold: (i) with the marker unset, the root's verdict is abstain; and (ii) the dir the marker names is a member of R5's candidate set for that same root. Observation that decides it: with the marker unset, record the verdict AND R5's candidate set; the cell counts only if the verdict is abstain AND the marker-named dir appears in that set; then set the marker through the channel under test, replay the byte-identical payload, and assert the verdict is DENY carrying the marker-subject attribution R25(b) requires. A root satisfying (i) but not (ii) must be reported as an unusable fixture, never as 'this channel does not reach the hook' - which is the reading that would otherwise reverse R25.

vulnerabilities.description: R21(c)'s residual sentence - shipped verbatim into ten files, and restated in the tracking issue #111 - discloses TWO abstention branches ('when ZERO records are in flight, OR when TWO OR MORE are and neither a marker nor the mtime scan discriminates among them') and then attaches ONE remedy to both: 'propagating an explicit active-issue signal closes it'. The remedy provably closes only the second branch. R25(a) honours a marker only when the record it names is itself in-flight per R5, and a zero-candidate root has no such record BY CONSTRUCTION, so no marker can ever lift that branch out of abstention. Measured (C5, pinned resolver ce7961e): zero in-flight records, marker set to name the sole (concluded) record, activeIssueDir resolves it to 106 while the R5-narrowed resolution stays ABSTAIN. The branch the marker cannot close is also precisely the state residual (f)/#110 produces - a live Phase 4 delta round whose record still carries the prior round's final_verdict, alone in its root, yields zero candidates - so the shipped text tells a reader that the residual they are most likely to hit on this repo's own known lifecycle bug is closed by #111, when it is not. R21's own closing line makes this its stated failure mode: 'a residual sentence that ... names a remedy this spec's own rules forbid is the claim-MORE defect'. The rule that forbids it is R25(a), which AC38 was re-pinned this round to test, so the two cannot both be relaxed.
vulnerabilities.location: spec.json requirements R21 clause (c); mirrored in github.com/nsmedia-io/agent-pipeline issue #111 ('That ruling means a marker can turn an abstention into a resolution, which is exactly what closes residual (c)')
vulnerabilities.remediation: For EACH abstention branch the residual sentence discloses, the sentence must state whether the named remedy closes THAT branch, and the zero-in-flight branch must be stated as NOT closed by the active-issue marker. Observation that decides it: build a root holding zero in-flight records, set the marker to name a record in that root, replay a payload that would otherwise be denied, and read the verdict; if the verdict is abstain while the shipped sentence claims the remedy closes that state, the sentence is false. The same correction is owed to #111, which currently inherits the claim.

vulnerabilities.description: Answer to the round-6 security question, recorded as a finding-of-no-finding because it is the question I was dispatched on. R4's record-content-first ordering creates NO new way to manipulate which record wins ownership, and it net-CLOSES one channel. Enumerated by CLASS rather than by example, all measured against the pinned resolver: (class 1) shrink the candidate set to zero by writing final_verdict into, or backdating updated_at past IN_FLIGHT_MS in, the run's own status.json - one field, one Write, gate abstains (C2); (class 2) enlarge the candidate set with a decoy, either undatable-and-newest so nothing may own the deny (C4, = R21(e)'s worked example) or datable-newest at a non-Phase-4 phase so the decoy becomes the resolved owner and the gate affirmatively believes a false phase (C3); (class 3) mtime-only disarm, needing NO content write at all - tie the newest status.json mtimes with one touch, or let a fresh Linux clone do it, and the shipped activeIssueDir returns null. Classes 1 and 2 are content-based, predate round 6 (they are R5's, not R4's), and behave identically before and after the reordering. Class 3 is the one round 6 changes, and it CLOSES it: R4(2) makes a sole in-flight candidate the owner 'whatever the mtime scan says, including when it abstains on a tie' (C1: activeIssueDir -> null, R5 candidates -> ['106'], verdict DENY; non-zero control, tie broken by 60s -> activeIssueDir -> 106, verdict DENY). So an agent with write access to its own status.json CONTENT gains nothing it did not already have, and the reordering removes the only disarm that content access was not required for. The floor on the cheapest attack rises; the ceiling is unchanged.
vulnerabilities.location: spec.json requirements R4 'RESOLUTION ORDER, FIXED IN ROUND 6'; verified against plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:327-368 at origin/main ce7961e

vulnerabilities.description: Posture note, not a defect. After round 6 the gate's subject resolution rests entirely on fields an actor inside the dispatch worktree can write, since mtime is no longer an independent co-authority. Both directions of candidate-set manipulation ARE disclosed - R21(e) covers enlargement and R21(f) covers the final_verdict exclusion - so the artifact is honest and I am not blocking. The gap is framing: (f) presents the final_verdict exclusion purely as a lifecycle BUG, so a reader takes away the accident and not the adversary, and (e)'s cost claim ('no parseable updated_at') describes only the undatable variant while the datable-decoy variant (C3) costs the same and resolves rather than abstains. The gate is a ratchet against an accidental blanket commit, not a control against a hostile agent that already holds Write - which is the correct scope and is what R21(e)'s 'disclosure, not a fix requirement' already concedes.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Optional. If (e)'s wording is touched for any other reason, state the class rather than the one worked variant, so a reader does not infer that a decoy with a parseable updated_at is outside it.

Conditioning the abstention on a TIE means a non-tie with two candidates RESOLVES via the mtime scan. R21(c) restates it: the gate enforces nothing only 'when TWO OR MORE are and neither a marker nor the mtime scan discriminates among them'. ba_notes restates it a third time. Under that reading the fixture above resolves to the '4-review' record and DENIES. AC12(i) asserts the identical fixture is NOT DENIED and names 'resolve from the newest-mtime dir regardless of ownership' as a mutation that MUST REDDEN it. AC30(c) asserts the two-in-flight root abstains and that the MARKER is what turns it into a deny. AC41 cell (i) asserts, for a root with a '3-impl' candidate and a re-dated '4-review' candidate, 'the verdict stays NOT DENIED' and only the attribution changes. AC38's whole matrix takes 'abstain' as the baseline for a one-'3-impl' + one-'4-review' root and asserts the marker 'MAY go from abstain to deny'.

An implementer who reads R4 ships a gate that reddens AC12(i), AC41(i) and AC30(c). An implementer who reads the criteria ships a gate for which R4(4)'s 'the mtime scan may select among them' is dead code and R21(c)'s parenthetical is false. Both pass their author's own review.

concerns.title: AC26 enumerates the shared seams as living in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, which R6 explicitly contradicts for the in-flight/datability predicate, and it supplies a behavioral discriminator for only one of the four seams R16 names.

ISSUE_DIR_RE still comes from the shared module, so AC26's only behavioral cell stays green. AC4 asserts the strip's OUTPUT ('pipeline:ba' and 'ba' attribute equal and non-empty), which a faithful private copy satisfies on the day it ships - which is exactly the failure mode R16 cites from voice-lint.mjs's private /^\d+$/. Every criterion in the spec stays green with the copy in place.

concerns.title: Fourteen citations of the form 'commands/pipeline.md:<n>' name a path that does not exist from the repository root, and AC33's checking population is restricted to 'README.md:<n>' - so exactly the citation family that is wrong today is the one nothing checks.
concerns.measurement: In the isolated tree at ce7961e: `ls commands/pipeline.md` -> 'No such file or directory'. `find . -name pipeline.md -not -path './.git/*'` -> ./plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md (1291 lines). The LINE NUMBERS are correct against that path and I verified them: :90-92 is the checkpoint pair inside the bash fence (AC3), :95 is the dependency note (R22/AC32), :812 is the Phase 4 tracked-write isolation block (problem statement), :997 writes 4-veto-rework-required with veto_reason, :1010 writes 4-review-complete with final_verdict.
concerns.why_it_binds: R20 exists because 'two different files in this repo are called README.md', and it demands 'every citation in the shipped artifacts and comments must carry the path, so following it reaches the literal rather than the wrong file's EOF'. A path that resolves to ENOENT is the same defect one step worse. AC33 discharges R20 only over 'README.md:<n>' references. I confirmed the README citations all open: plugins/pipeline/README.md:142 = 'The three hooks have a dependency-free bash suite', :148 = 'It builds throwaway git repos and drives each hook end to end', :84 = the item-6 paragraph carrying 'a halting control with an opt-out knob is not a halting control', root README.md:24 = the hooks/ tree listing. The family that opens is the family that is checked; the family that does not open is the family that is not.
concerns.cost_if_unfixed: R22/AC32 instruct the implementer to edit 'commands/pipeline.md:95'. Followed literally from the repo root that is a no-op, and AC32 has no mechanical check that the edit landed in a file that exists.
concerns.what_must_be_true: AC33's population is every '<path>:<n>' citation in the shipped artifacts, comments and this spec - not the README subset - and the assertion is that the named path OPENS and the named line contains the attributed literal. The spec's own commands/pipeline.md citations are rewritten to plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md.

concerns.title: The new 'evaluate EVERY git invocation in a compound command' rule creates a command-splitting surface, and no negative population is stated for it: a '&&' or ';' inside a quoted operand.
concerns.derivation: R7(ii) fixes the rule that a compound command is decomposed into git invocations and any one deny denies the whole call. Decomposition is a parser, and a parser's failure direction here refuses correct work. AC7's compound cells are both positives. AC9 says 'for every row of AC7 there is a paired allow fixture in which that exact literal occurs inside a non-operative operand', which covers the compound rows only by a blanket that names no cell.
concerns.constructible_input: `git commit -m "chore(pipeline): the Phase 4 block now bans git add . && git commit -a (#106)"`. A splitter that cuts on && without honouring quoting yields a second invocation `git commit -a (#106)`, which matches the blanket-flag class, and the call is DENIED. This is not a synthetic string: R7's own first paragraph says 'this issue's own ten-file doc retirement produces exactly that commit', and the retired sentence at plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:812 literally contains 'never `git commit -a`, `git add -A` or `git add .`'.
concerns.what_must_be_true: AC7 carries a named negative cell for each compound separator - a quoted '&&', a quoted ';', and a quoted '|' - asserted NOT denied, with the mutation 'split on the separator without honouring quoting' required to redden them and nothing else. Without it a naive splitter passes the whole suite and refuses the commit that ships this very issue.

concerns.title: AC11's '4-review-complete' deny cell is unreachable in production: the writer sets that phase and final_verdict in the same update, so R5 excludes every real record at it.
concerns.evidence: plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md:1010 - 'Update status.json with current_phase: "4-review-complete", final_verdict, and a peer_review_verdict_counts object'. R5 evaluates final_verdict FIRST and excludes unconditionally. Corroborated on the corpus: both committed records at that phase carry one (.pipeline/56 APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, .pipeline/exp-script-test-coverage REQUEST_CHANGES). By contrast :997 writes '4-veto-rework-required' with veto_reason and NO final_verdict, so THAT cell is genuinely reachable and it carries R12's real harm.
concerns.impact: The cell still catches the `phase === '4-review'` mutation, so R12's fix is not lost. But the criterion presents it as a behavioural assertion about a live phase and it is an assertion about a shape the writer never produces. AC15 already applies exactly this discipline to '4-review-round-2' ('may appear only if explicitly labelled a synthetic future-suffix probe'); AC11's third cell deserves the same label, and the fixture must be stated as carrying no final_verdict or it fails for a reason unrelated to the phase term and invites an implementer to 'fix' the phase check.

findings.title: A live input defeated the gate: the tokenizer was super-quadratic in command length, so a padded commit message crossed the declared 5s hook timeout and the blanket commit was ALLOWED
findings.root_cause: _scan walked the command one character at a time and each step cost three parameter expansions over the WHOLE remaining string. The same two idioms -- `${s#"$long"}` (drop a prefix by naming it) and `${s%"${s#?}"}` (read the first character) -- also sat in _js_get and _js_unescape, which is why the cost was still ~2.4s each in those two after _scan alone was fixed. Both idioms are quadratic in bash, /bin/sh and dash: measured over a 32000-char subject, 10 calls each, against a 72ms empty-loop floor -- `${s#"$pre"}` 22151ms, `${s%"${s#?}"}` 20524ms, `${s#*|}` 6423ms, against 75ms for `${s#<512 literal ?>}` and 176ms for `${s%%[|]*}`.
findings.fix: One shared `_cut` helper drops a prefix in fixed-width steps (512/64/8/1) whose patterns are compile-time constants; every first-character read became an anchored `case`; `_scan` takes runs of ordinary characters in one bulk slice per METAcharacter; the short-option cluster loop is anchored; and `_word_done`/`_head_kind` stop the scanner hoarding positional parameters for an invocation already settled as non-git.

qa_bypass_cell_git_commit_a_m_padded.2500: 5.014s rc=124 KILLED, no output, ALLOWED -> 0.199s DENY

findings.residual_recorded_not_fixed: A SINGLE git invocation's own operands must still be hoarded, because _eval_inv decides _pathspec/_blanketspec over the whole list, so the N-squared survives for that one shape. Measured: `git add . <N operands>` = 0.79s at N=500, 2.4s at 1000, 8.8s at 2000, 34.0s at 4000, so past roughly 1400 operands the deny crosses the timeout and fails open. Recorded in the source beside _word_done. Closing it means hoisting the operand classification out of _eval_inv into the scan loop, which is a redesign rather than a fix; flagged to QA/BA for its own issue.

findings.title: A trailing shell redirection or `#` comment turned `git add -A` (and friends) from DENY back into ALLOW
findings.root_cause: _scan treated only `; & | newline ( )` as separators, so `>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>`, their targets, and every word after `#` fell through into the word list. _eval_inv then classified the non-dash operand as a pathspec, and `if [ "$_verb" = commit ] || [ "$_pathspec" = 0 ]` used that to decide the add/stage command was narrow. The commit branch short-circuits before _pathspec is consulted, which is why `git commit -a -m x > /dev/null` kept denying and hid the hole.
findings.fix: Redirection operators (`>`, `>>`, `>|`, `>&`, `<`, `<<`, `<&`, `<>`), their fd-number prefixes (`2>`) and their targets are recognised and never reach the operand walk; `#` at a word start opens a comment to end of line, while `#` inside a word stays an ordinary character.
findings.before_after: 66-row table (11 FORBIDDEN spellings x {bare, ' > /dev/null', ' 2>/dev/null', ' >/dev/null 2>&1', ' >>out.log', ' # note'}), driven through the real hook with CLAUDE_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE=106: BEFORE 36 deny / 30 allow (every add/stage row with metatext allowed); AFTER 66 deny / 0 allow. Controls held: `git add -u plugins/pipeline/agents/dba.md` allow, `git status --porcelain` allow, `git add -u <path> > /dev/null` allow, `git add foo#bar` allow, `git add -A | cat` deny, `git commit -a -m x > /dev/null` deny.

findings.title: A backslash LINE CONTINUATION defeated the gate outright: `git add -A \<newline> && git commit -m "x"` returned NO decision while a real bash staged and committed every file
findings.root_cause: `_lit1`'s `"$_NL"*) _w=$_w$_NL ;;` arm appended a LITERAL newline to the current word when it saw a backslash-newline pair. POSIX DELETES backslash-newline before tokenizing -- it is not a character, not a word and not a word boundary -- so the arm manufactured an operand the shell never creates. One operand is the whole of the term that downgrades an `-A`/`-u` stage from blanket to narrow, so the verdict flipped to `clear`. The commit branch never consults that term, which is why `git commit -a \` kept denying and hid it, exactly the asymmetry that hid the redirection hole one round earlier.
findings.fix: Both backslash arms in `_scan` (outside quotes AND inside double quotes) consume the pair and emit nothing, leaving `_has` untouched so the words either side JOIN the way the shell joins them. `_lit1`'s newline arm is deleted, and the comment that claimed it was needed is deleted with it, because for newline that sentence was not true. A lone trailing backslash also produces no word, matching what bash does.

findings.title: The scan cost was driven by WORD-BOUNDARY COUNT, not string length, and the round-2 fix addressed only length

root_cause_three_separate_quadratics_eac.1_positional_hoard: `set -- "$@" "$_w"` rebuilds the whole word list per append. That append ALONE, isolated: 347 ms at k=500, 1195 at 1000, 4807 at 2000, 19658 at 4000, 78780 at 8000. This is what made `git add . <2000 operands>` take 8.3 s.
root_cause_three_separate_quadratics_eac.2_per_call_positional_save: A shell function call SAVES AND RESTORES the positional parameters, so calling anything per word while a large list is live costs the list's LENGTH: a `for` walk over k fields calling one function per field measured 219 ms at k=500, 714 at 1000, 2699 at 2000, 10466 at 4000, against 68-99 ms for the same walk with NO call at any k. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS FIX DID EXACTLY THAT and made the 5000-word shape SLOWER (8901 ms) than the 3305 ms it set out to remove. Recorded because it is the trap, not a footnote.
root_cause_three_separate_quadratics_eac.3_cursor_move_per_word: Every cursor move copies what is left of the command, and `_cut`'s `?`-at-a-time rung cost one whole copy per CHARACTER of the prefix -- four copies for a four-character word.

findings.fix: The judge takes every word of an invocation in ONE call and folds them with `for f do`, with nothing inside the loop being a function call (which is why the head-word and operand tests are written inline and `_head_kind` is gone). The scan loop advances once per STRUCTURAL character and hands each whitespace-separated run to the shell's own field splitting under `set -f` with IFS pinned to space and tab. `_cut` drops its <64-character residual by NAME in one pass. `_cut_sc` removes the two extra whole-string copies the `_CUR` protocol cost on the scanner's hot path. A blanket pathspec short-circuits the whole scan the moment it is seen.
findings.fix_second_site: `_js_unescape` had the SAME defect on the same deciding path, keyed on ESCAPE count rather than word count -- a multi-line command carries one `\n` escape per line, and it measured 215 ms over a 20 KB value, 609 over 40 KB and 2165 over 80 KB. It now splits on the escape character in one pass, reading the EMPTY field as `\\`.

findings.title: The basename de-dup hands the decision to root order when two same-named copies disagree, and nothing tested it
findings.dba_reproduction_does_not_reproduce: DBA reported that pairing a fresh in-progress copy with a CONCLUDED one produces DENY in one root order and abstains in the reverse. It does not: run through `resolveRunOwner` directly, `[in-flight 4-review, concluded]` and `[concluded, in-flight 4-review]` BOTH resolve to 4-review, because `inFlightObservations` gives `candidate: !concluded && ...` so a concluded record is never a candidate and never claims the name. The concluded record ALONE does abstain, which is correct. THE FINDING SURVIVES ANYWAY at a different pair: two NON-concluded copies at different phases -- `[4-review, 3-impl]` resolves to 4-review (deny) and `[3-impl, 4-review]` resolves to 3-impl (no deny). That is the pair QA named.
findings.resolution: No new tiebreak was invented, per DBA's own instruction. The precedence that decides it already exists and is already documented at pipelineDirs: 'Most-specific root first: the stopping agent's own cwd is where ITS artifacts live.' The payload cwd is the tree the calling agent is working in, so its copy describes the run the call belongs to. That is now ASSERTED with an ORDER TWIN that swaps the roots and requires the verdict to swap, on copies with genuinely different content and with a vacuity control that fails if a future edit makes them identical again. Reversing the root list reddens both rows (it survived 402 assertions before).

the_surviving_residual_filed_as_116.mechanism: POSIX sh has no bounded cursor: every parameter expansion or `case` over the remaining command copies the WHOLE remainder. The scan turns once per STRUCTURAL character, so its cost is (structural characters) x (length). A MULTI-LINE command is the reachable instance, because every line-ending newline is structural. Separately, `_cut`'s ladder is O(p^2 / 512) in the prefix, which bites on one very long token.

items_addressed.title: A phantom operand survives in the one spelling that actually stages files: an unquoted expansion that vanishes from argv
items_addressed.what_was_wrong: `_inv_words` counted ANY non-empty word after the verb as a pathspec, and one pathspec is the whole term that downgrades `git add -A` from blanket to narrow. Round 3 closed the LITERAL empty string, which real git refuses outright (exit 128, stages nothing), and left the word that the shell DELETES before git is executed, which stages everything.
items_addressed.the_fix: An operand carrying an unresolved substitution is OPAQUE and may not narrow, at both operand positions (ordinary, and after `--`). The test is over the CLASS -- POSIX sh introduces a substitution with exactly two characters, `$` and the backquote, and every spelling of parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic necessarily contains one -- not over a table of spellings. It sits at the operand position ONLY: a word opening with a dash is still read for its flag letters, so `git add -A$X` and `git commit -a$X` still deny.
items_addressed.verification_method: SecOps own stated observation, run rather than read. Each row was driven (a) through the SHIPPED hook exactly as hooks.json declares it, with a subagent payload and one in-flight 4-review record under an isolated cwd, and (b) through /bin/sh -c with a recording git shim first on PATH that prints the argv the SHELL really produced, and (c) through /bin/sh -c against a REAL scratch git repository holding one modified tracked file and two untracked ones, reading `git diff --cached --name-only` plus the new commit file list when HEAD moved.
items_addressed.before_at_36831f4: All 21 forbidden rows returned NO DECISION (ALLOWED). Representative: `git add -A $NOPE` -> hook none; real shell ARGC=2 [add] [-A]; scratch repo exit 0, staged tracked.txt + untracked_a.txt + untracked_b.txt. Same for ${NOPE}, ${NOPE:-}, $(true), $(echo), backquoted, $NOPE $NOPE, -u/--all/--update/stage variants, EMPTY="", WS="   ", CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only), `-- $NOPE`, redirection- and comment-tailed, cd-prefixed and `git -C .`-prefixed.
items_addressed.after_at_12a15f3: 23 of 23 forbidden rows deny; 8 of 8 allow twins still allow; zero mismatches. The suite figure moved 329 -> 583 in test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh with 0 failed.
items_addressed.oracle_asymmetry_that_names_the_right_ha: `git add -A ''` reaches git as a real EMPTY third argument (ARGC=3 [add] [-A] []) which git refuses, exit 128, nothing staged. `git add -A $NOPE` reaches git as ARGC=2 -- the word is gone -- and stages every file. Refusing the literal prevented no staging; the vanishing one is the whole harm.

items_addressed.cost_stated_rather_than_hidden: CORRECTED IN ROUND 5, and the correction is the finding. The round-4 wording said: `git add -A foo$X` and `git add -A '$literal'` "both stage NOTHING in a real shell (exit 128), so no successful staging is refused". THAT CLAIM IS FALSE FOR THE CLASS, and both QA and SecOps falsified it independently. Both fixtures chosen use an UNSET variable, so exit 128 is a property of those two fixtures, not of the class shipped. THE ACTUAL COST, re-measured by Dev in a scratch repository holding a modified packages/pipeline/a.txt, an untracked packages/pipeline/new.txt and an untracked outside.txt: `sh -c 'PKG=pipeline; git add -A packages/$PKG'` exits 0, stages packages/pipeline/a.txt and packages/pipeline/new.txt and leaves outside.txt alone -- a successful, correctly NARROWED stage that this gate now denies; `sh -c 'F=packages/pipeline/a.txt; git add -u "$F"'` exits 0 and stages exactly that one file, also denied. Control on the same fixture: bare `git add -A` stages all three. So the class is: A BLANKET FLAG BESIDE ANY OPERAND CARRYING AN EXPANSION IS REFUSED, INCLUDING ONE THAT RESOLVES TO A REAL PATH AND WOULD HAVE STAGED A CORRECTLY NARROWED SET -- `git add -A "$ARTIFACT_DIR"`, `git add -A .pipeline/$ISSUE`, `git add -u "$DIR"` are the same shape, and SecOps measured 416 of 488 executable new-deny rows carrying a real pathspec in argv. WHY IT IS ACCEPTED RATHER THAN FIXED: `$F` holding a real path and `$F` holding nothing are THE SAME TEXT to a scanner that never sees argv, so refusing the first is the price of denying the second and no ordering of a text scan separates them. Both panelists state the deny is forced and correct and neither asks for a code change. WHAT BOUNDS THE COST: the refusal is loud, carries its reason, and is rewritable two ways that are both allowed and both now asserted in the suite -- name the path literally (`git add -A packages/pipeline` -> none) or drop the blanket flag (`git add "$DIR"` -> none); and a repository-wide grep for a blanket flag beside an expansion-bearing operand returns only prose ABOUT this trade-off, zero real consumers, so no work this repository does today is actually refused. The same correction is carried in the hook's own residual text (pre-tool-use.sh, the `_inv_words` WHAT IT COSTS block), and the over-denial now has SEVEN asserted cells (three DENY, two allowed-rewrite bounds, two recording-shim ORACLE rows proving the denied operand really does resolve to a narrowing pathspec) where round 4 had prose only.
items_addressed.residual_disclosed_and_asserted: An opaque operand is refused the power to NARROW; it is NOT credited with the power to BLANKET. `git add $X` with X=`.` is therefore not seen. Crediting it would refuse `git add $FILE`, the ordinary correct command. The direction is deliberate: an empty expansion is an ACCIDENT its author did not intend, while X=`.` is a blanket stage its author chose, and this text-scanning gate never claimed to refuse a stage somebody meant to write. Both halves are asserted in the suite (two `ALLOW, disclosed residual` rows), so the choice is a decision and not a silence.
items_addressed.overclaim_narrowed_per_secops: The `_inv_words` comment round 3 added ("AN OPERAND COUNTS AS A PATHSPEC ONLY IF IT NAMES SOMETHING ... a word that narrows nothing narrows nothing") is replaced by one that states both halves and which was live. The suite title `AC7 EMPTY OPERAND: a word that names nothing narrows nothing` is now `AC7 EMPTY OPERAND: a LITERAL empty string is not a pathspec`, with a paragraph saying the vanishing word is a different fixture tested in the block below.

items.finding: The `_inv_words` header stated a class wider than the test: 'POSIX sh has exactly TWO characters that introduce a substitution ... a word whose final content is not determined by the text cannot be read as naming a path'. Pathname expansion is a POSIX word expansion, is not a substitution, contains neither character, and under nullglob erases the word.
items.action_taken: DISCLOSURE IN THE TREE (the first of the two options SecOps offered), and BOTH halves of it. The class sentence is NARROWED to the substitutions it actually implements ('a word whose final content is decided by a SUBSTITUTION cannot be read as naming a path'), and a new paragraph 'WHAT THAT SENTENCE DOES NOT COVER' names pathname expansion as outside it, with both argv readings, the gate verdict beside each, and the reason. The wrong fix SecOps named is explicitly refused in the text: adding `*` to the opaque set would move the control back to reading spellings and would refuse `git add -A *.md` where the glob resolves.
items.dev_re_measurement: Reproduced by Dev with a recording git shim first on PATH, in a directory holding a.txt and b.txt, on darwin 25.5.0 / bash 3.2.57(1)-release. `bash -c 'shopt -s nullglob; git add -A *.nope'` -> ARGC=2 [add] [-A]; gate verdict ALLOW. Gate verdicts measured in the same batch as a `git commit -a -m "x"` -> deny control.

infra_changes.summary: Adds a PreToolUse(Bash) entry, command resolved from ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, matcher 'Bash', timeout: 5 (seconds, per the runtime's own E=H.timeout*1000/EL=600000 in Claude Code 2.1.85, cited in spec.json R1/AC1). Well under the 600s ceiling, single-digit magnitude as the spec requires. Fallback in the declared command ('|| { echo ...; exit 0; }') fails open on any non-zero rc from the hook script itself.

New two-stage gate: stage 1 (this file, no shebang by deliberate measurement) is pure POSIX sh, reads Bash tool payload, classifies staging commands (add/stage/commit) into blanket-vs-narrow via a tokenizing scanner, and only escalates to node when a blanket-staging class is found AND agent_id is present. Fails open on every tooling gap with an attributed stderr note.

Stage 2: resolves run ownership (resolveRunOwner) and Phase-4 guardedness, emits a PreToolUse hookSpecificOutput deny JSON on stdout with exit 0 when a Phase-4-owned run is found; abstains (exit 0, stderr note, no stdout) on every ambiguous/tooling-gap branch. Never receives the caller's command text (only cwd/agent_type/active_issue), by design, to avoid publishing user-controlled text to a child process argv/env other local users can read.

New leaf module exporting inFlightObservations()/IN_FLIGHT_MS, deliberately dependency-free of both validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs and gate-phase-entry.mjs to avoid closing the module cycle gate-phase-entry.mjs already has at :71 (import of activeIssueDir). gate-phase-entry.mjs's own inFlight() now delegates to it, passing its own IN_FLIGHT_MS export explicitly so the #63-mutation-pinned declaration site is unchanged.

Exports pipelineDirs, activeIssueName, bareRole, resolveRunOwner (previously private/duplicated). resolveRunOwner is a NEW shared-contract function: candidate narrowing across .pipeline roots (symlink-resolved dedup via realpathSync), marker-vs-inference provenance, ambiguous-owner abstention. checkArtifacts's own bareAgentType logic was refactored onto the new exported bareRole (behavior-preserving, confirmed by validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's own passing self-test, 25/25).

One residual NOTED, not blocking: my very first pass through the new suites (a sequential loop, then a bare `run.sh`) produced wildly inconsistent results -- test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh initially read 64 passed/83 failed with nearly every DENY-class row failing, and a subsequent `run.sh` invocation hung past a 2-minute timeout. `ps aux` at that moment showed 5+ OTHER `bash .../tests/run.sh` processes already running from sibling worktrees (tmp.3RKlKrXndJ, tmp.XGpAn6rY5p, tmp.NSQ3z5VK28, PIDs started 10:05-10:14) -- i.e. other Phase 4 panelists dispatched alongside me on this SAME physical host, each independently running this identical CPU-bound suite. This tracks: test-pretooluse-gate-declaration.sh's AC18 block explicitly measures wall-clock cost (20x sh -c ':' loops, dozens of real node cold starts) and asserts a bounded DIFFERENCE against a same-run baseline -- a design that already self-corrected once ('Round 8 retired the absolute 3x-of-baseline bound... a threshold on a rendered measurement measures the runner') but is still, by construction, sensitive to CPU contention on whatever host runs it. I could not reproduce a false failure running in isolation, and GitHub Actions' ubuntu-latest runs one job per VM rather than five identical concurrent CPU-bound suites, so I have no evidence this flakes in the actual CI environment -- only that it flakes under the adversarial concurrency this review session itself created. Not filing a new deferred issue for this: it would be speculative without CI evidence, and the existing AC18 design already carries an EXPIRY control and a live non-zero control per its own comments. Flagging it here so a future CI red on this suite is diagnosed as 'noisy runner, re-run' before it is diagnosed as 'gate broke'.

OBSERVATION THAT DECIDES IT: take the sentence's own claim -- here 'no successful staging is refused' -- and run the recording-shim oracle over the newly-denied rows with the variable SET to an existing path; the claim holds only if no denied row's real argv both carries a narrowing pathspec and exits 0 having staged only that path. vulnerabilities.description: THE FIX'S OWN STATED CLASS IS BROADER THAN ITS TEST, AND THE GAP IS MEASURABLE. CWE-693 (protection mechanism failure) / OWASP A04 insecure design, same family as the round-3 finding and the same defect SHAPE: a comment claiming a closure the code does not earn. `_inv_words` now says 'THE TEST IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A TABLE OF SPELLINGS ... POSIX sh has exactly TWO characters that introduce a substitution -- `$` ... and the backquote ... So the rule is over the CLASS: a word whose final content is not determined by the text cannot be read as naming a path.' PATHNAME EXPANSION is a POSIX word expansion that is not a substitution, contains neither character, and produces a word whose final content is decided by the FILESYSTEM rather than by the text -- and under `nullglob` it DELETES the word, which is the same argv erasure the whole round-4 fix exists to close. MEASURED on darwin 25.5.0 / bash 3.2.57(1) / git 2.52.0, with a recording git shim first on PATH: `bash -c 'shopt -s nullglob; git add -A *.nope'` in a directory holding a.txt and b.txt hands git `ARGC=2 [add] [-A]` -- a full blanket stage -- and the shipped hook, driven exactly as hooks.json declares it with an in-flight 4-review record, returns ALLOW. NON-ZERO CONTROL on the same fixture, so this is a reading and not a silence: with nullglob OFF the identical string hands git `ARGC=3 [add] [-A] [*.nope]`, a real pathspec, and git then exits 128 having staged nothing -- which is why this is NOT reachable on a default host and is graded medium rather than high. SCOPE, checked rather than assumed: `grep -rn 'nullglob|pathname expansion'` over pre-tool-use.sh, test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh and spec.json returns nothing, and #118 does not name it either, so this is an undisclosed member of the class rather than a scoped-out one. REACHABILITY, graded honestly against evidence.md's ship-or-block line: a LIVE INPUT can defeat it (one Bash call, no privilege, no future edit), but the adversarial path is already subsumed by #118 -- `eval "git add -A"` is cheaper and is filed -- so what this adds is the ACCIDENTAL path on a host where nullglob is on: `git add -A *.json` in a directory with no JSON becomes a blanket stage, which is precisely the accident class the gate exists for. It is a claim-MORE defect in evidence.md's sense: the comment's stated class covers this and the code's test does not.
vulnerabilities.location: plugins/pipeline/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh, the `_inv_words` header block ('POSIX sh has exactly TWO characters that introduce a substitution' / 'a word whose final content is not determined by the text cannot be read as naming a path'); plugins/pipeline/tests/test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh, suite 'AC7 OPAQUE OPERAND', whose OPAQUE_OPERANDS list is nine substitution spellings and no filesystem-resolved one.
vulnerabilities.remediation: PROPERTY: where a control's own text states the CLASS it closes, every word expansion that can erase or replace an operand before git sees it must be either inside the test or named as outside it -- a stated class strictly wider than the implemented test is the defect, whichever way it is narrowed. OBSERVATION THAT DECIDES IT: run the fix's own recording-shim oracle over one row per POSIX word-expansion kind (parameter, command, arithmetic, and PATHNAME expansion under `shopt -s nullglob`) and compare the recorded argv against the gate's verdict; for every row whose recorded argv carries a blanket flag and no pathspec, the gate must either DENY it or the hook's residual text must name that expansion kind as out of scope, with the argv reading beside it. At 12a15f3 the pathname row returns `ARGC=2 [add] [-A]` against a gate verdict of ALLOW and no text anywhere names it, so neither branch is satisfied. THE HALF THAT IS CHEAP AND SO IS STATED IN THE PROPERTY: the substitution half is already true and re-running `$NOPE`/`$(true)`/`` `true` `` is not evidence for this -- I measured all 30 of those rows denying and agreeing with the oracle. The unsatisfied half is the expansion that carries NEITHER character. THE TELL, stated because it decides what a correct close looks like without naming one: if the answer is to add `*` to the opaque-character set, the control has moved back to reading spellings of the input, and it would also refuse `git add -A *.md` in a directory where that glob resolves -- real narrowing work. DEFERRING IS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME HERE and is probably the right one, because the default-shell reachability is zero and the adversarial path is #118's: the deferral is discharged only when the residual is WRITTEN, before this merges, either as a paragraph in the hook's own residual text or appended to #118, carrying (a) the two argv readings above (nullglob on -> ARGC=2, off -> ARGC=3), (b) the gate verdict beside each, and (c) the reason the two-character structural argument does not reach it -- AND the sentence 'a word whose final content is not determined by the text cannot be read as naming a path' is narrowed to the substitutions it actually implements, because a general sentence over a specific test is what made the next reader stop looking in round 3.

concerns.title: The round's own stated COST is falsified by a one-command measurement: impl-report.json says 'no successful staging is refused', and `PKG=pipeline; git add -A packages/$PKG` exits 0, stages two files, and is DENIED by the shipped gate

evidence.the_sentence: impl-report.json, on the acknowledged over-denials: "Two acknowledged over-denials, both measured: `git add -A foo$X` and `git add -A '$literal'` are now denied although a real shell hands git a pathspec for each. Both stage NOTHING in a real shell (exit 128), so no successful staging is refused; the only correct work refused is a blanket flag beside a variable path, and the narrow form `git add $FILE` is untouched." The two clauses of that sentence contradict each other, and the false one is the one a reader triages on.
evidence.the_measurement_that_falsifies_it: Real git 2.x, scratch repository at /private/tmp/qa106r4/scratch (its own repo, not a worktree here), holding one modified tracked file and two untracked ones, one of each under packages/pipeline/ and one outside it. `sh -c 'PKG=pipeline; git add -A packages/$PKG'` -> exit 0. `git diff --cached --name-only` -> packages/pipeline/a.txt, packages/pipeline/new.txt. `git status --porcelain` -> outside.txt still `??`. That is a SUCCESSFUL, CORRECTLY NARROWED stage. The shipped gate at 12a15f3 denies it: my driver returns `deny` for `git add -A packages/$PKG`.
evidence.the_class_is_wider_than_the_two_fixtures: Also DENY at 12a15f3, every one of them a blanket flag scoped to a computed path that a real shell resolves to a genuine narrowing pathspec: `git add -A "$ARTIFACT_DIR"`, `git add -A "$ARTIFACT_DIR/peer-review.qa.json"`, `git add -A .pipeline/$ISSUE`, `git add -u "$DIR"`, `git add -A "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/src"`. The two fixtures the report names (`foo$X`, `'$literal'`) both happen to use an UNSET variable, which is why both exit 128 -- so 'exit 128' is a property of the two fixtures chosen, not of the class shipped. This is the same failure mode as my round-3 QA-R3-2, one position over: a cost figure that is a property of its fixture population.
evidence.the_asymmetry_that_makes_it_a_coverage_p: The UNDER-denial residual (`git add $X` with X=`.` is not seen) is asserted with two ALLOW cells, and I proved under mutation M4 that they bite. The OVER-denial has NO cell anywhere in the suite -- it lives only in prose in the hook comment and the impl-report. So the two halves of the same disclosed trade-off get opposite treatment: one is a decision the suite defends, the other is a sentence nothing observes. A later change that widened or narrowed the over-denial would not redden anything.
evidence.direction_and_reachability: CLAIM-LESS, which is why this is a note and not a blocker. The defect can only produce MORE refusals; a refusal is visible, is returned with a reason, and the agent can rewrite (`git add "$DIR"` without the blanket flag is allowed, verified). It ships no falsehood into any output. And my repo-wide grep found ZERO in-repo commands of the shape, so the realized cost today is nil. What is wrong is the RECORD: the sentence claims more than the measurement supports, in the artifact a future reader will use to decide whether the trade was worth it.
evidence.the_correct_work_this_guardrail_refuses_: `git add -A <computed-directory>` / `git add -u "$DIR"` -- 'stage every change under this path, whose name I computed'. That is ordinary correct work, it is refused, and nothing in the repository writes it today.

what_would_close_it: The FILING half: correct impl-report.json's 'no successful staging is refused' to what the measurement supports, and state the class as 'a blanket flag beside an operand carrying an expansion' with one successful-staging example, so the cost cannot be re-read later as two harmless exit-128 curiosities. The hook's own comment at pre-tool-use.sh:355-359 should carry the same correction; it currently presents the two unset-variable fixtures as WHAT IT COSTS.

The COVERAGE half: one asserted DENY cell for the over-denial, e.g. `git add -A packages/$PKG` and `git add -u "$DIR"`, titled as a DELIBERATE over-denial with the real-shell outcome recorded beside it -- the same treatment the two residual ALLOW rows already get. Then both halves of the trade-off are decisions the suite defends rather than one decision and one sentence. I am naming the missing test, not writing it; this routes to Dev.

Neither is a code change and neither should hold the merge on its own. If the orchestrator prefers, the coverage half is legitimately a follow-up issue -- but then it must be WRITTEN there before this merges, with the `PKG=pipeline` measurement in it, per deferring-is-an-action.

concerns.title: One new assertion is green for a reason its own name contradicts: `--$X` never becomes end-of-options, it matches the unknown-long-option arm

evidence.the_row: test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh: `assert_eq "DENY: git add -A --\$X (an expansion attached to \`--\` is still end-of-options)"`. The verdict is correct; the explanation is not.
evidence.the_discriminator_i_ran_rather_than_reas: If `--$X` set end-of-options, the next word would be read as an OPERAND (narrowing -> none); if it is just an unknown long option, the next word is still read as a FLAG (blanket -> deny). Driven at 12a15f3: `git add -A -- -u` -> none (so `--` really does make `-u` an operand, my positive control) but `git add -A --$X -u` -> deny (so `--$X` did NOT set end-of-options; `-u` was read as a blanket flag). Confirmed in the source: `--)` matches only the exact two-character word, and `--$X` falls through to the `--*)` arm at pre-tool-use.sh:388 which ignores it without touching `_endopts`.
evidence.why_it_is_only_a_nit: No behaviour is wrong. With X unset a real shell hands git `add -A --`, a blanket stage, and the gate denies; with X set to anything, git errors on an unknown option and nothing is staged, so the deny costs nothing. The defect is that the row's NAME asserts a mechanism the code does not implement, so a reader counts an end-of-options-through-expansion case as covered when no such path exists. A comment is a claim: either the code earns the sentence or the sentence comes out.
